authors: David Janz, Arya Akhavan, Alexandre B. Tsybakov
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish general upper bounds on the maximum effective dimension and information gain of kernel Gram matrices over arbitrary designs in terms of approximation properties of the kernel or, equivalently, of the corresponding reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We show that across three regularity regimes, covering as special cases the Mat\'ern and squared exponential kernels, these bounds cannot be improved beyond constant factors.
tldr: This paper establishes general upper bounds on the maximum effective dimension and information gain of kernel Gram matrices over arbitrary designs, based on approximation properties of the kernel.
motivation: Effective dimension and information gain of kernel matrices are key quantities in kernel methods and learning theory, and the authors aim to provide unified bounds across different kernel regularity regimes.
method: The authors derive upper bounds using approximation properties of the kernel or the corresponding reproducing kernel Hilbert space, covering Matérn and squared exponential kernels as special cases.
result: Across three regularity regimes, the bounds are shown to be optimal up to constant factors, meaning they cannot be improved asymptotically.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for bounding effective dimension and information gain, with implications for kernel-based learning algorithms.

title: Multilevel Fair Allocation Under Additive Preferences
authors: Maxime Lucet, Nawal Benabbou, Aur\'elie Beynier, Nicolas Maudet
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study multilevel fair resource allocation with tree-structured hierarchical relations among agents. At each level, the problem can be viewed locally as allocating an agent's bundle to its children, the overall allocation being a trace of this process iterated down to the leaves. Assuming that internal nodes' utilities are the utilitarian welfare of their children, and the leaves have classical additive utilities over items, we first propose multilevel adaptations of usual envy-based fairness notions (e.g., WEF1). We present three adaptations and show that the choice among them is not neutral. We prove that, under identical preferences, the three adapted envy-based notions coincide, and that the Multilevel extension of Weighted Round Robin (Chakraborty et al., 2021) (MWRR) guarantees them. We then show that under general preferences, MWRR may guarantee some notions while failing others. Finally, through experiments, we show that MWRR may still perform well even for adaptations it does not formally guarantee.
tldr: This paper studies fair resource allocation in hierarchical agent structures, proposing multilevel envy-based fairness notions and analyzing an algorithm (MWRR) that guarantees them under certain conditions.
motivation: In hierarchical settings like organizations, fair allocation should respect the tree structure, but standard fairness notions do not apply directly; hence the need for multilevel adaptations.
method: The authors define three variants of multilevel envy-freeness, prove relationships among them, analyze the guarantees of the Multilevel Weighted Round Robin (MWRR) algorithm, and conduct experiments.
result: Under identical preferences, the three adapted envy-based notions coincide and MWRR guarantees them; under general preferences, MWRR guarantees some but not others, though experiments show it performs well even for unguaranteed notions.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational analysis of fairness in hierarchical allocation, highlighting trade-offs between different adaptations and offering practical guidance for algorithm choice.

title: QisMC: A Model Checker For Qiskit Program Debugging
authors: Mingsheng Ying Aochu Dai
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present QisMC, the first quantum model checker dedicated to debugging Qiskit programs. On the theoretical side, we introduce the notion of quantum-classical transition system and a quantum computation tree logic (qCTL) grounded in Birkhoff-von Neumann logic for modeling the behaviors and specifying the properties of Qiskit programs, respectively. On the implementation side, QisMC provides an end-to-end framework encompassing transition system generation, logical formula representation, and model checking algorithms, and it efficiently performs image computation based on decision diagrams. These methods and design principles give QisMC advantages over previous Qiskit program debuggers, including a unified property specification language, a fully automated and exhaustive verification process, and the ability to generate counterexamples. Extensive illustrative examples and benchmark evaluations demonstrate the practicality, efficiency, and scalability of QisMC in verifying realistic quantum programs.
tldr: QisMC is a model checker for Qiskit programs using quantum-classical transition systems and quantum computation tree logic.
motivation: Existing Qiskit debuggers lack automated and exhaustive verification; this paper aims to provide a unified, rigorous approach.
method: Introduces quantum-classical transition systems and qCTL logic based on Birkhoff-von Neumann logic, with model checking algorithms using decision diagrams.
result: Demonstrates efficiency and scalability on benchmarks, and can generate counterexamples.
conclusion: QisMC is the first model checker for Qiskit, offering a fully automated verification process and unified property specification language.

title: A Theory Of Finite-Noise Optima And Generalization In Quantum Machine Learning
authors: Ziyu Zhang, Zikang Jia, Xiaosong Li, Yulong Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum noise is expected to degrade quantum machine learning by driving circuits away from their noiseless implementations. Yet recent studies show moderate noise can reduce testing error, a behavior unexplained by weak-noise perturbative error accumulation or strong-noise trainability collapse. Here we develop a statistical learning theory connecting microscopic noise processes to macroscopic learning performance. At its heart is a noise-order purity parameter, derived from a surrogate model analysis, that predicts the noise-induced reduction in model complexity and the consequent reduction in the generalization gap. Noise simultaneously increases prediction bias. Their competition explains the intermediate-noise regime left open between these limits. It produces a finite-noise optimum whose location depends on the learning setup and can disappear in the large-sample limit. Numerical experiments validate these predictions. Noise programming can move a model towards this optimum. These results make the non-monotonic effect of noise predictable and provide a route to harness it.
tldr: The paper develops a statistical learning theory for quantum machine learning that explains and predicts the non-monotonic effect of noise on generalization, yielding a finite-noise optimum.
motivation: Moderate quantum noise can surprisingly reduce testing error, which is unexplained by existing perturbative or trainability-collapse theories; this work aims to connect microscopic noise to macroscopic learning performance.
method: A noise-order purity parameter is derived from a surrogate model analysis, and a statistical learning framework is built to predict noise-induced changes in model complexity and generalization gap.
result: Noise reduces model complexity and generalization gap but increases prediction bias, leading to a finite-noise optimum whose location depends on the learning setup and may vanish in the large-sample limit; numerical experiments confirm these predictions.
conclusion: Noise programming can be used to move a model toward the optimum, making the effect of noise predictable and potentially harnessable in quantum machine learning.

title: Lexicographic Social Ranking On Monotonic Coalitional Rankings
authors: Stefano Moretti Felix Fritz
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent studies on social rankings in coalitional settings have introduced methods that rank individuals by lexicographically comparing vectors of their occurrences across coalitions ordered according to their strength. In this work, we focus on two such solutions: the lexicographical excellence (lex-cel) solution, which disregards coalition size, and the L^(1) solution, which additionally prioritizes smaller coalitions through a double lexicographic comparison. We investigate the combinatorial connections between these two solutions on monotonic coalitional rankings, where equivalence classes are compactly represented through sets of minimal (with respect to set inclusion) coalitions. After introducing general formulas for computing the lex-cel and L^(1) parameter vectors from these minimal coalitions, we also present worst-case running time results. Finally, to further explore the behavior of the two solutions through simulations designed to assess the distance of the rankings they produce, we show that the monotonicity assumption does not lead to actual redundancy in the rankings produced by the two solutions.
tldr: This paper studies two lexicographic social ranking methods for monotonic coalitional rankings, deriving computational formulas and showing non-redundancy of monotonicity.
motivation: To understand combinatorial and computational properties of lexicographic social ranking rules on coalition structures, particularly under monotonicity constraints.
method: The authors formalize lex-cel and L^1 ranking rules, provide closed-form expressions for parameter vectors using minimal coalitions, analyze worst-case running times, and run simulations to compare output rankings.
result: They derive general formulas, establish worst-case time complexities, and demonstrate that the monotonicity assumption does not cause redundancy in the generated rankings.
conclusion: The work contributes to social choice and game theory, but is outside the scope of quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Artifact Side Peaks In Saturated Absorption Spectroscopy Caused By Inappropriate Lock-in Amplification
authors: Leo Matsuoka
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Saturated absorption spectroscopy is a powerful technique that provides valuable information about gas-phase atomic targets, including not only the precise positions of transitions but also the effects of velocity-changing collisions, which manifest as changes in the shape of the peaks. However, using a lock-in amplifier inappropriately can generate artifact side peaks, potentially leading to a misinterpretation of results. To investigate the emergence of these artifacts, we conducted numerical calculations based on the basic Lambert-Beer's law. Our model reproduced the artifact side peaks and revealed that these artifacts become more significant as the transmittance of the probe laser decreases.
tldr: This paper studies artifact side peaks in saturated absorption spectroscopy caused by improper lock-in amplifier usage, using numerical simulations.
motivation: Inappropriate lock-in amplification can generate artifact side peaks in saturated absorption spectroscopy, leading to misinterpretation of results.
method: Numerical calculations based on Lambert-Beer's law were performed to model the emergence of artifact side peaks.
result: The model reproduced the artifact side peaks and showed they become more significant as probe laser transmittance decreases.
conclusion: Artifact side peaks must be considered to avoid misinterpretation in saturated absorption spectroscopy measurements.

title: A Comment On Local Hypercube Inequalities
authors: Keyou Zhuo, Tian-Shun Chen, Kilar Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This comment gives dimension-independent analytic proofs of the local inequalities arising in the odd- and even-dimensional constructions of higher-dimensional partition charge functions. The prior works established these inequalities by exhaustive computation in low dimensions and tested them numerically in selected higher dimensions.
tldr: Provides dimension-independent analytic proofs of local inequalities from higher-dimensional partition charge functions, replacing prior computational checks.
motivation: Prior works relied on exhaustive computation in low dimensions and numerical tests in higher dimensions, leaving a gap for analytic proofs.
method: The paper gives analytic proofs that work for arbitrary dimensions, covering both odd- and even-dimensional constructions.
result: Establishes the inequalities rigorously without dimension-specific computation.
conclusion: The inequalities are proven analytically, strengthening confidence in the constructions.

title: Weak Irreducibility As A Spectral Criterion For Phase Coexistence
authors: Onofre Rojas
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional finite-size theories describe first-order coexistence through free-energy competition and interfacial tunneling, but the distinct spectral roles of sector balance and inter-sector connectivity are not usually explicit. We show that pseudo-transitions and thermodynamic phase coexistence are governed by two spectral coordinates: sector imbalance locates balance, while connectivity determines whether that balance remains avoided. At balance, finite connectivity produces a unique dominant state with equal spectral weights in the symmetrized two-sector representation. For short-range systems with positive interface tension, interfacial costs suppress the connectivity exponentially, close the coexistence splitting, and asymptotically restore reducibility. Thus, genuine phase coexistence emerges as the singular limit of finite-size avoided coexistence, whereas one-dimensional pseudo-transitions retain finite connectivity. In a decorated bilayer Ising model, the coexistence gap at independently est.
tldr: The paper introduces a spectral criterion based on weak irreducibility to distinguish genuine phase coexistence from pseudo-transitions in finite-size systems.
motivation: To clarify the distinct roles of sector balance and inter-sector connectivity in first-order phase coexistence, which are not explicit in conventional finite-size theories.
method: Analytically and numerically analyzes the spectrum of a decorated bilayer Ising model using two spectral coordinates: sector imbalance and connectivity.
result: Finite connectivity yields a unique dominant state with equal spectral weights at balance, while exponentially suppressed connectivity closes the coexistence splitting and restores reducibility.
conclusion: Genuine phase coexistence emerges as a singular limit of avoided coexistence, whereas pseudo-transitions retain finite connectivity.

title: Hartree--Fock Coercivity For Twisted Bilayer Graphene
authors: Maciej Zworski Kevin D. Stubbs
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the minimisers of the Hartree--Fock functional for flat bands in the chiral model of twisted bilayer graphene introduced by Tarnopolsky, Kruchkov, and Vishwanath. Our model is a continuous version of the discrete model considered by Becker, Lin and Stubbs in previous works and the first result is a direct analogue of main theorems of those papers: at half filling of the flat band of multiplicity two, there are exactly two minimisers, obtained by occupying either one of the two sub-bands. (A more general version of this result, stressing its topological origins, was presented in Appendix A.8 of the Lecture Notes by Tao-Zworski.) The new contribution is the strict coercivity of the Hessian of the Hartree--Fock functional at the two minimisers. It is a consequence of the difference between the Chern numbers of the component bands and can be optimistically considered as a soft version of a ``spectral gap''.
tldr: This paper studies the Hartree-Fock functional for the chiral model of twisted bilayer graphene, proving the existence of exactly two minimisers at half-filling and the strict coercivity of the Hessian.
motivation: To understand the mathematical structure of electron interactions in twisted bilayer graphene, specifically the nature of ground states at half-filling of the flat band.
method: The authors analyze a continuous version of the chiral model, examine the Hartree-Fock functional, and use topological arguments involving Chern numbers to establish the results.
result: At half filling, there are exactly two minimisers corresponding to occupying either of the two sub-bands, and the Hessian is strictly coercive due to the difference in Chern numbers.
conclusion: The strict coercivity provides a soft spectral gap for the Hartree-Fock functional, offering insight into the stability of the ground states.

title: Macroparticles With Different Weights Relax To Different Temperatures In Particle-In-Cell Simulations
authors: Remi Lehe, Arianna Formenti, Justin R. Angus, Jean-Luc Vay
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A distinctive feature of Particle-In-Cell (PIC) simulations is the use of macroparticles, each representing many physical particles. The associated macroparticle weight can vary from one species to another, or even from one macroparticle to another. Here we show that, when macroparticles have different weights, the plasma evolves toward an unphysical thermal equilibrium in which the temperatures are unequal: lower-weight macroparticles reach a higher temperature than physically expected, and higher-weight macroparticles a lower one. We show that this unphysical equilibrium is difficult to avoid, but that reaching it takes time, and that the associated timescale depends on the effective collisionality of the PIC algorithm. We derive an equation that predicts the full time evolution of the temperatures, in good agreement with PIC simulations, and use it to identify strategies to delay the establishment of this unphysical thermal equilibrium.
tldr: Shows that in PIC simulations, macroparticles with different weights relax to different temperatures, creating an unphysical thermal equilibrium, and provides a predictive equation and mitigation strategies.
motivation: To investigate and correct artifacts in PIC simulations caused by variable macroparticle weights, which lead to incorrect temperature equilibration.
method: Analytical derivation of an equation for temperature evolution, validated against PIC simulations.
result: Demonstrates unequal temperatures for different-weight macroparticles, matches simulations with the derived equation, and identifies strategies to delay equilibrium.
conclusion: The unphysical equilibrium is hard to avoid but can be delayed; the equation helps predict and mitigate this issue.

title: Quantum Algorithms And Hardness For Point-Count Approximation Over Finite Fields
authors: Hiroshi Yano Yota Maeda
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the approximation of the number of solutions of Laurent polynomials over finite fields. For a Laurent polynomial \[f(x)=\sum_{j=1}^{s}a_jx^{u_j}\in _q[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_n^{\pm1}], \] let [MATH] be its augmented support matrix whose columns are [MATH] with rank [MATH] and [MATH] be its torus point count. Our first main result is a quantum algorithm that outputs [MATH] satisfying \[ |(f) - N(f)| \le \varepsilon q^{n+s/2-\rho} \] with success probability [MATH]. Provided that [MATH] and [MATH] are bounded, the algorithm runs in both classical bit and quantum gate complexity [MATH]. It provides finer resolution than relative-error approximations in general settings. To the best of our knowledge, in the explicit finite-field input model considered here, no previous algorithm achieves this additive accuracy with running time polynomial in [MATH]. Van Dam (arXiv:quant-ph/0405081) conjectured the existence of such an algorithm under the assumption of an oracle reflecting the algebraic properties of the polynomial. In contrast, by exploiting a point-counting formula derived from character sums over finite fields, we develop an alternative approach that efficiently approximates the number of points without assuming the existence of such an oracle. As a second main result, we prove that the same approximation problem becomes [MATH]P-hard under randomized polynomial-time Turing reductions when the support matrix [MATH] varies freely as part of the input. Thus, taken together, our results clarify how the effectiveness of the quantum approach depends on the tradeoff between the accuracy scale and the support parameters of the input polynomial.
tldr: The paper presents a quantum algorithm for approximating the number of solutions of Laurent polynomials over finite fields with additive error, and proves the problem is #P-hard when the support matrix varies.
motivation: To efficiently approximate point counts over finite fields, which has applications in algebraic geometry and cryptography, given limitations of previous algorithms and a conjecture by Van Dam.
method: The algorithm uses character sums over finite fields to derive a point-counting formula and exploits this without requiring an oracle; hardness is shown via randomized polynomial-time Turing reductions.
result: The algorithm runs in polynomial time for bounded parameters and achieves additive accuracy, while the problem becomes #P-hard when the support matrix varies freely.
conclusion: The results clarify the tradeoff between accuracy and support parameters, indicating when quantum efficiency is possible and when the problem is computationally hard.

title: Bulk Phase Transition And Edge Behavior In Temporally Correlated Random Matrices
authors: Takuya Kaneko Masato Hisakado
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study long-range correlated Wigner-type matrices built from row-independent stationary Gaussian sequences. For exponentially decaying (AR(1)) correlations, the bulk spectral density deforms from the semicircle law via an explicit combinatorial "hub" mechanism, yet we verify the flatness and decay hypotheses of the matrix-Dyson-equation framework (MDE), with numerical evidence supporting Tracy-Widom edge universality for every fixed [MATH] of the exponential decay correlations; the degenerate limit [MATH] reduces to a symmetrized Volterra operator, connecting to the singular-value cascade identified in a companion BBP analysis. For power-law correlations [MATH], we identify [MATH] as the critical point for divergence of the bulk fourth-moment, while [MATH] marks the breakdown of the flatness condition governing the MDE edge analysis. We prove the fourth-moment transition exactly and find numerically that the self-consistent edge varies smoothly across [MATH], with no evidence of a kink or discontinuity.
tldr: This paper analyzes spectral properties of correlated random matrices, focusing on bulk phase transitions and edge behavior.
motivation: To understand how temporal correlations affect the spectral density and edge universality in Wigner-type matrices.
method: Uses explicit combinatorial mechanisms, verifies flatness conditions from matrix-Dyson-equation framework, and performs numerical simulations.
result: Identifies critical points for fourth-moment divergence and flatness breakdown, proves the fourth-moment transition, and shows smooth edge behavior across the critical point.
conclusion: Provides insights into phase transitions in random matrix ensembles with correlations, connecting to Volterra operators and singular-value cascades.

title: Time-Dependent Tunneling In The Thin-Barrier Limit
authors: Tanmay Vachaspati, Frank Wilczek, Zara Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The usual WKB analysis for quantum tunneling applies when the tunneling action is large, as it is for tall, wide potential barriers. In contrast we analyze tunneling when the action is small, as it is for tunneling across a tall, thin barrier. We develop a perturbative analysis where the control parameter is the inverse of the area under the potential barrier and apply our technique to several examples in [MATH] dimensions. In resonant situations for bound particles we find that the tunneling probability grows with time as [MATH], while in non-resonant situations it grows linearly with time. We evaluate not only the tunneling probability but also the time-dependent tunneling wavefunction for a particle that escapes to infinity, {\it i.e.} from a quasi-bound state to the continuum.
tldr: A perturbative analysis of quantum tunneling through thin barriers when the tunneling action is small, yielding time-dependent tunneling probabilities and wavefunctions.
motivation: To extend tunneling analysis beyond the WKB regime of large action, focusing on thin, tall barriers where the action is small and standard approximations fail.
method: Developed a perturbative expansion in the inverse of the barrier area, applied to several examples in multiple dimensions, distinguishing resonant and non-resonant cases.
result: Tunneling probability grows quadratically with time in resonant situations and linearly in non-resonant situations; the time-dependent wavefunction for escape to infinity is computed.
conclusion: Provides a new analytical framework for thin-barrier tunneling, revealing distinct temporal scaling behaviors and enabling explicit wavefunction evaluation.

title: Mesa Orientation Engineering For Polarization Locking In VCSELs
authors: Zifeng Yuan, Wenkai Shan, Tingting Chen, Beibei Lin, Aaron Danner
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While polarization stability is common in many optical systems, intentional polarization bi-stability is also important for polarization-encoded computing. We propose a mesa orientation strategy to engineer the polarization switching of vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs). Further experiments demonstrate improved polarization locking performance.
tldr: This paper proposes a mesa orientation strategy for engineering polarization switching in VCSELs to achieve improved polarization locking performance.
motivation: To achieve intentional polarization bi-stability for polarization-encoded computing.
method: Proposing a mesa orientation strategy and conducting experiments to demonstrate its effectiveness.
result: Experiments demonstrate improved polarization locking performance.
conclusion: The mesa orientation strategy is effective for engineering polarization switching in VCSELs, beneficial for polarization-encoded computing applications.

title: Efficient Treatment Of Non-Linearity In Quantum Computational Fluid Dynamics Using Hybrid Tensor Networks
authors: Pia Siegl, Nis-Luca van H\"ulst, Maximilian Mandelt Buxad\'e, Tomohiro Hashizume, Dieter Jaksch
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear terms present a fundamental challenge for quantum computational fluid dynamics, as their implementation on inherently linear quantum hardware typically requires resource-intensive workarounds that limit scalability to large-scale simulations. We present a hybrid quantum-classical tensor network algorithm that addresses this bottleneck by combining variational time-stepping with quantum tensor programming to efficiently compile operators and time-dependent fields into quantum circuits. Within a probabilistic framework, we replace prior state-based nonlinear implementations with tensor-based block encodings, stabilizing success probabilities that otherwise decay exponentially with system size. Benchmarking on turbulent flow fields demonstrates that the algorithm maintains high success probabilities and moderate measurement overhead across increasing Reynolds numbers and grid resolutions. Compared to fully classical tensor network solvers, our hybrid approach yields substantial reductions in both memory footprint and computational cost, establishing a scalable pathway toward practical quantum advantage in scale-resolving CFD simulations.
tldr: Presents a hybrid quantum-classical tensor network algorithm for quantum computational fluid dynamics that efficiently handles nonlinear terms using tensor-based block encodings.
motivation: Nonlinear terms are a fundamental challenge for quantum computational fluid dynamics on linear quantum hardware, requiring resource-intensive workarounds that limit scalability.
method: The algorithm combines variational time-stepping with quantum tensor programming to compile operators and time-dependent fields into quantum circuits, and uses tensor-based block encodings to replace prior state-based nonlinear implementations.
result: Benchmarking on turbulent flows shows high success probabilities and moderate measurement overhead across increasing Reynolds numbers and grid resolutions, with substantial reductions in memory and computational cost compared to classical tensor network solvers.
conclusion: The hybrid approach establishes a scalable pathway toward practical quantum advantage in scale-resolving CFD simulations.

title: Boundary Free Energies, Quenched Mixing, And Gibbs-State Selection In Disordered Ising Models
authors: Mauris Chueng, Hexiang Wang, Keheng Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study boundary free energies and half-space responses in nearest-neighbor disordered Ising models. First, we prove the existence of fixed-depth tangential pressure and identify its derivative almost everywhere with the limiting boundary response. Second, under quenched exponential boundary-response mixing, we prove Gibbs-state selection independence and exponential convergence of finite-depth pressures. We further show that uniform one-spin mixing yields DLR uniqueness and Gaussian normal localization, and verify the required mixing conditions whenever [MATH]. Finally, we establish an all-face surface limit in the bounded Dobrushin regime and provide counterexamples that delimit general surface and stiffness claims.
tldr: The paper analyzes boundary free energies and Gibbs-state selection in disordered Ising models, providing rigorous results on pressure derivatives and mixing conditions.
motivation: Understanding boundary effects and Gibbs-state selection in disordered systems is important for characterizing their thermodynamic behavior.
method: The authors use rigorous mathematical analysis, including fixed-depth tangential pressure, quenched exponential mixing, and the bounded Dobrushin regime, to derive properties.
result: They prove the existence of fixed-depth tangential pressure, Gibbs-state selection independence under mixing, and verify required conditions in certain cases, while providing counterexamples that delimit general claims.
conclusion: The results clarify boundary responses and uniqueness of Gibbs states under specific mixing conditions, but general surface and stiffness claims are limited.

title: Nonlocal-nonlinear Phonon Polaritons
authors: Gonzalo \'alvarez-P\'erez, Line Jelver, Alexander Paarmann, Simone de Liberato
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When light is confined to deeply subwavelength volumes, optical responses can become nonlocal. Yet how nonlocality reshapes nonlinear light-matter interactions remains largely unexplored, particularly in dielectrics. Here, we theoretically uncover a new class of nonlinear optical processes arising from the interplay between optical-phonon propagation and ionic-bond anharmonicity in polar crystals. We show that, unlike conventional local nonlinearities, this mechanism enables second-order responses even in centrosymmetric materials. Moreover, these responses can be tuned by the confinement and resonantly enhanced near optical-phonon resonances. Using density functional perturbation theory, we quantify the resulting nonlocal second-order susceptibilities in representative polar crystals. Our results establish nonlocal-nonlinear optics as a new regime of light-matter interaction in dielectrics.
tldr: The paper introduces nonlocal-nonlinear optical processes in polar crystals, enabling second-order responses even in centrosymmetric materials.
motivation: To explore how nonlocality reshapes nonlinear light-matter interactions in dielectrics, a largely unstudied regime.
method: Uses density functional perturbation theory to compute nonlocal second-order susceptibilities in representative polar crystals.
result: Shows that nonlocal nonlinearities are tunable by confinement and resonantly enhanced near optical-phonon resonances, yielding second-order responses in centrosymmetric materials.
conclusion: Establishes nonlocal-nonlinear optics as a new regime of light-matter interaction in dielectrics.

title: Measurement Of The O$^{-}$ Photodetachment Cross-section In The Electrostatic Storage Ring Flsr
authors: Oliver Forstner, Thorben Niemeyer, Andrey I. Bondarev, Markus Dworak, Vadim Gadelshin, Raphael Hasse, Lothar Schmidt, Markus Sch\"offler, Matou Stemmler, Kurt E. Stiebing, Dominik Studer, Klaus Wendt, Patric Ziel
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The achievable precision of photodetachment studies via tunable laser light has been investigated on circulating oxygen anions at the room-temperature electrostatic low-energy storage ring of Frankfurt University (FLSR) in preparation of investigations on molecular species. For this purpose, the FLSR, originally designed for reaction dynamics studies on positive ions, was upgraded by a source for anions, by the installation of a tunable high repetition rate laser system and by implementation of a transversal interaction region between laser and ion beam. Results on the electron affinity and the ground state fine structure of O[MATH], which both serve as a calibration standard, are discussed, exhibiting the performance and accuracy of this new spectroscopic application of the FLSR.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-precision photodetachment spectroscopy of oxygen anions using an upgraded electrostatic storage ring, providing calibration standards for future molecular studies.
motivation: The authors aimed to prepare the FLSR storage ring for photodetachment studies on molecular species by upgrading it for anionic beams and laser interaction.
method: They upgraded the FLSR with an anion source, a tunable high-repetition-rate laser, and a transversal interaction region, then measured photodetachment cross-sections of O-.
result: They obtained measurements of the electron affinity and ground state fine structure of O- that match calibration standards, showcasing the performance and accuracy of the setup.
conclusion: The FLSR is now viable for high-precision spectroscopic studies on anions, with future applications to molecular species.

title: Abstracts: Amsterdam Benchmark Suite For The Time And Resource Analysis Of Clifford+T Simulators
authors: John van de Wetering Matthew Sutcliffe
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent years have seen a rapid growth in literature presenting new methods for simulating non-Clifford quantum circuits with classical hardware. These methods span a range of approaches, including stabiliser decomposition and tensor contraction techniques, varying in efficiency depending on circuit class, depth, non-Clifford gate count, and other metrics. A notable limitation of this literature is the lack of a standardised approach to benchmarking, with each new paper outlining its own specification, simulating its own set of circuits on the authors' own hardware. This paper seeks to address this issue by presenting a standardised and canonical benchmark suite and infrastructure for quantifying the efficiency of non-Clifford classical simulators, with a consistent dataset of circuits and providing consistent (virtual) hardware, thereby enabling a fair comparison of results.
tldr: This paper introduces a standardized benchmark suite for comparing classical simulators of non-Clifford (Clifford+T) quantum circuits.
motivation: The lack of standardized benchmarking in the literature for non-Clifford circuit simulators hinders fair comparison.
method: They provide a canonical benchmark suite with a consistent dataset of circuits and a virtual hardware setup.
result: The suite enables fair and reproducible comparisons of simulator efficiency.
conclusion: It offers a common framework to assess and improve classical simulation methods for quantum circuits.

title: Algorithmic Cost In "Exact Real Computation"
authors: Jihoon Hyun, Holger Thies, Martin Ziegler
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Turing completeness of a programming language or system characterizes its expressive power; and the strong Church-Turing hypo-/thesis refines such from qualitative to polynomial-time equivalence. Exact Real Computation (ERC) is a novel numerical programming language paradigm: for the imperative processing of continuous data as entities appearing as exact, i.e. devoid of rounding errors [doi:10.1007/978-3-662-44199-2_107]. ERC has been designed [doi:10.46298/lmcs-20(2:17)2024] as convenient and practical alternative, namely proven qualitatively equivalent, to the Turing machines originally underlying Computable Analysis [doi:10.1007/978-3-642-56999-9,doi:10.1007/978-1-4684-6802-1]. The present work quantitatively strengthens this qualitative Turing-completeness: We assign bit-costs to ERC's operational primitives (including partial/multivalued tests) in such a way that any real function incurring polynomial cost becomes Turing-computable in polynomial time, and vice versa. Runtime measurements on implementations in the iRRAM C++ library confirm our theoretical performance predictions.
tldr: The paper establishes a quantitative bit-cost model for Exact Real Computation and proves polynomial-time equivalence to Turing machines.
motivation: To strengthen the theoretical foundations of Exact Real Computation (ERC) by providing a rigorous cost measure, complementing its known qualitative Turing-completeness.
method: The authors assign bit-costs to operational primitives of ERC, including partial/multivalued tests, and prove that a real function is computable in polynomial time under this model iff it is Turing-computable in polynomial time.
result: Any real function incurring polynomial cost becomes Turing-computable in polynomial time and vice versa, with runtime measurements from iRRAM C++ library confirming theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work quantitatively bridges ERC and classical computability, offering a formal cost equivalence that can guide future implementations and complexity analyses.

title: The Completion Of A Continuous Inverse Algebra Need Not Be A Continuous Inverse Algebra
authors: Zongjian Han
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2006 Neeb asked whether the Hausdorff completion of a continuous inverse algebra must again be a continuous inverse algebra. The noncommutative case remained open, while the commutative case was known to be true. We give a negative answer after twenty years. We construct a Hausdorff metrizable locally m-convex complex continuous inverse algebra whose completion is a Fr\'echet locally m-convex algebra, where inversion stays continuous but the set of invertible elements is not open. The construction uses finite-support sequences in a dense nil subalgebra of a Jacobson-semisimple Banach algebra. Finite support makes every element nilpotent, giving continuous inversion without a locally uniform bound on nilpotence indices. In the completion, shifting a fixed noninvertible element to later and later coordinates produces noninvertible elements converging to the identity. Thus completion destroys exactly the local spectral stability at the identity. The counterexample is necessarily noncommutative and marks the precise boundary of the commutative completion theorem.
tldr: This paper constructs a counterexample showing that the Hausdorff completion of a continuous inverse algebra need not be a continuous inverse algebra, answering a question by Neeb.
motivation: To resolve an open question posed by Neeb in 2006 about the preservation of the continuous inverse algebra property under Hausdorff completion in the noncommutative case.
method: Uses finite-support sequences in a dense nil subalgebra of a Jacobson-semisimple Banach algebra, ensuring every element is nilpotent and inversion is continuous without a locally uniform bound on nilpotence indices.
result: Constructs a Hausdorff metrizable locally m-convex complex continuous inverse algebra whose completion is a Fréchet locally m-convex algebra, where inversion remains continuous but the set of invertible elements is not open.
conclusion: Provides a negative answer to Neeb's question, demonstrating that the commutative case does not extend to the noncommutative setting.

title: On Split Forms Of Fusion Categories
authors: C\'esar Galindo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate split Galois descent for fusion categories through framed equivalences, reducing the existence of a split form to a group-theoretic splitting problem. The associated degree-two obstruction combines categorical coherence with stable descent of the simple objects, while fusion spaces impose index and parity restrictions. For quantum groups at roots of unity, we use the quasi-[MATH]-matrix to make the bar involution tensor-compatible and prove that the underlying fusion category [MATH], associated with the simply connected root datum, has a split form over the maximal totally real subfield of the cyclotomic field generated by the quantum parameter. The same holds for all its cyclotomic Galois conjugates; in particular, every [MATH] has a split real form. By contrast, no split real form exists for the standard braiding except on [MATH] and [MATH], [MATH]. We further show that associative zesting can destroy real descent of [MATH], while every braided zesting of [MATH] still admits a split real form as an underlying fusion category. Applications to pointed and finite-group representation categories give criteria for real descent in terms of cohomology and Frobenius--Schur indicators.
tldr: This paper studies split Galois descent for fusion categories, establishing splitting criteria and applying them to quantum group categories at roots of unity.
motivation: To understand when fusion categories arising from quantum groups admit real forms, which is a question in mathematical physics and algebra.
method: It formulates split Galois descent via framed equivalences, reduces to a group-theoretic problem, and uses obstruction theory and categorical coherence.
result: It proves that certain quantum group fusion categories have split real forms and studies stability under zesting, with applications to pointed and finite-group categories.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for real descent of fusion categories, with implications for quantum symmetry structures.

title: Let AEDs Move: Urban Mobility Enhanced Defibrillator Deployment
authors: Bahar Dehqani Viniche, Sheng Liu, Nooshin Salari
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Timely access to automated external defibrillators (AEDs) remains a major limitation of public-access defibrillation systems because stationary AED networks cannot adapt to spatial and temporal variation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) demand. We study a platform-enabled mobile AED model in which AEDs are carried by existing urban ride-hailing fleets that can be dispatched to OHCA locations. Rather than assuming additional AED capacity, we hold the total AED supply fixed and compare alternative allocations between stationary and mobile deployment, including hybrid policies that retain both forms of coverage. Our analysis leverages real-world urban data from New York City and Toronto, integrating georeferenced public AED inventories, EMS-reported OHCA incident data, and ride-hailing mobility data. The results show that mobile AEDs can substantially improve both response times and reliability, but the benefits depend on how AED capacity is divided between stationary and mobile deployment. In New York City, average response-time gains exceed 2.5 minutes and peak when approximately 55 to 70 percent of AED capacity is mobile; beyond this range, both gains and reliability decline as stationary coverage is reduced. In Toronto, average gains approach 4 minutes and then plateau as the system moves toward a fully mobile configuration. These contrasting patterns show that mobile AEDs can materially improve access, but the best mix of stationary and mobile AEDs must be tailored to local coverage and mobility conditions.
tldr: This paper studies the allocation of mobile automated external defibrillators (AEDs) on ride-hailing fleets to improve response times to out-of-hospital cardiac arrests, using data from New York City and Toronto.
motivation: Stationary AED networks cannot adapt to spatiotemporal variation in cardiac arrest demand, so the authors propose a mobile AED model using existing urban ride-hailing fleets to improve access.
method: The authors analyze fixed AED supply and compare stationary, mobile, and hybrid deployment policies using real-world data from NYC and Toronto, including public AED inventories, EMS-reported OHCA incidents, and ride-hailing mobility data.
result: Mobile AEDs can improve response times by over 2.5 minutes in NYC (optimal at 55-70% mobile capacity) and up to 4 minutes in Toronto, though the optimal mix depends on local conditions.
conclusion: Mobile AEDs can materially improve access to defibrillation, but the best deployment strategy must be tailored to local coverage and mobility patterns.

title: Asymptotically Tight Bounds For Generalized Covering Radii Of Binary Primitive Bch Codes At All Higher Orders
authors: Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy Zeev Vladimir Belinsky (yohananov)
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how few parity-check columns are needed to span several prescribed syndromes of a binary primitive BCH code of length [MATH], where [MATH] is the extension degree. For the four-error-correcting family, the second generalized covering radius is exactly [MATH] for [MATH], and it is either [MATH] or [MATH] for [MATH]. For every fixed error parameter, we give an explicit stable two-value bound for the second radius together with an arithmetic criterion for exactness. For every generalized-covering order [MATH], we also obtain explicit stable lower and upper bounds. Under an additional explicit field-size condition, their additive gap is bounded independently of [MATH] for every fixed [MATH], so the bounds are asymptotically tight as [MATH] grows. The upper bound is the natural common-core count whenever [MATH], and in general differs from it by a correction bounded independently of [MATH]. At order three this gives stable intervals for three through six errors. We further prove that, for three errors, every three-dimensional syndrome space confined to the highest coordinate has exact support size ten once [MATH]. A single self-contained completion-cover framework supplies both the exact second-order results and the asymptotically tight bounds at all higher orders.
tldr: This paper studies the generalized covering radii of binary primitive BCH codes, deriving asymptotically tight bounds at all orders.
motivation: The covering radius of error-correcting codes is a fundamental parameter; understanding it for BCH codes is important for coding theory.
method: The authors introduce a completion-cover framework to analyze the number of parity-check columns needed to span prescribed syndromes.
result: They obtain exact values for the second-order case and asymptotically tight bounds for higher orders, with gaps bounded independently of the field size.
conclusion: The results provide a comprehensive characterization of generalized covering radii for binary primitive BCH codes.

title: Dimensionless Controls Of Plasticity Under Alternating Tasks: From Evolutionary Biology To Continual Learning
authors: Owen Skriloff
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Plasticity under changing environments is central to both evolutionary biology and continual learning. Motivated by recent work on genotype--phenotype maps, we study a minimal deep-learning analogue where a network is trained alternately on two Boolean label sets, and ask which biological controls of plasticity survive the translation to gradient descent. Reinterpreting four proposed biological factors as quantities of training dynamics, we find the system reduces to two dimensionless controls: the task disagreement [MATH], the fraction of disagreeing labels, and the reach [MATH], the product of learning rate and switching period. We derive two bounds on plasticity: [MATH] alone fixes an extremal geometric floor on the utopia distance, while [MATH] and [MATH] jointly bound forgetting. Across 9,720 trajectories, an ANOVA confirms that [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] dominate, while the effect of neutral-set size (emphasized in the biological setting) is negligible. The optimal reach itself follows an approximate inverse power law [MATH], yielding a heuristic that sets the optimal reach [MATH] from the task disagreement alone. The analogy that survives is therefore dynamical rather than geometric, and our setting enables a view of plasticity through the lens of other driven systems in physics and engineering.
tldr: The paper explores plasticity in continual learning via biological analogies, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The work aims to translate biological concepts of plasticity into deep learning, studying how networks adapt to alternating tasks.
method: It trains networks on alternating Boolean label sets and analyzes dimensionless controls derived from training dynamics, using 9,720 trajectories and ANOVA.
result: Task disagreement and reach dominate plasticity, with an inverse power law for optimal reach; neutral-set size has negligible effect.
conclusion: The analogy between biology and learning is dynamical, but the paper holds no relevance to the requested research areas.

title: Existence Of Relaxed Equilibrium For Time-Inconsistent Mean Field Games: A Set-Valued Fixed Point Approach
authors: Zhou Zhou Zhenhua Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the existence of relaxed equilibria for finite-horizon continuous-time time-inconsistent mean field games. We work directly on the product space of relaxed feedback policies and population flows. The policy component is endowed with the stable topology of Young measures, while the population component is restricted to a compact convex set of Wasserstein-continuous flows with uniform moment and time-regularity bounds. For every policy-flow pair, we establish uniform Sobolev and H\"older estimates for the associated auxiliary value function and prove its stability under Young-measure convergence of policies and uniform Wasserstein convergence of population flows. We also establish continuity of the induced population-flow map. The latter requires a duality argument for the Fokker-Planck equations because Young-measure convergence yields only weak-[MATH] convergence of the controlled drifts. We then construct a set-valued best-response/consistency map with nonempty compact convex values and apply the Kakutani-Fan-Glicksberg fixed-point theorem. The resulting fixed point satisfies both the equilibrium response condition of the intra-personal game and the mean field consistency condition, , thereby establishing the existence of a relaxed equilibrium.
tldr: This paper proves the existence of relaxed equilibria for time-inconsistent mean field games using a set-valued fixed point approach.
motivation: The study of time-inconsistent mean field games is important for modeling dynamic decision-making with non-exponential discounting, but existence results for relaxed equilibria are lacking.
method: The authors work on a product space of relaxed feedback policies (Young measures) and population flows, establish stability properties of value functions and the population-flow map, and apply the Kakutani-Fan-Glicksberg fixed-point theorem to a set-valued best-response/consistency map.
result: They prove the existence of a relaxed equilibrium satisfying both intra-personal equilibrium and mean field consistency conditions.
conclusion: The paper provides a rigorous existence result for a broad class of time-inconsistent mean field games, extending known fixed-point techniques.

title: Condition Numbers Of Block Toeplitz Matrices And Stability Of Space-time IgA Approximations For The Wave And Schr\"odinger Equations
authors: Manuel Bogoya, Albrecht B\"ottcher, Matteo Ferrari, Sergei M Grudsky, Stefano Serra-Capizzano
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In previous work by several authors, the behavior of the condition numbers of banded Toeplitz matrices was studied as the matrix size tends to infinity. In the present contribution, two main directions are pursued. As a first step, we extend this study to block Toeplitz matrices with blocks of fixed size [MATH]. As in the scalar case, we show that even when the symbol generates a Fredholm infinite Toeplitz operator, the condition numbers of the finite matrices may grow at least exponentially. Upper and lower bounds for the condition numbers are obtained, and examples showing that they may grow arbitrarily fast are presented. Then, as a second step, we apply the developed theory to the stability analysis of space-time Galerkin methods, where in time an Isogeometric approach is used with regularity [MATH], [MATH], [MATH] being the employed polynomial degree. These stability issues are related exactly to the conditioning of block Toeplitz-like matrices with blocks of size [MATH]. Specific examples are treated in detail and related numerical experiments are presented and critically discussed. We finally present a short list of relevant open problems.
tldr: This paper studies condition numbers of block Toeplitz matrices and applies them to stability analysis of space-time isogeometric approximations for wave and Schrödinger equations.
motivation: To extend previous work on scalar Toeplitz matrices to block Toeplitz matrices and use these results to analyze stability of numerical methods for PDEs.
method: The authors derive upper and lower bounds on condition numbers of block Toeplitz matrices, provide examples showing exponential growth, and apply the theory to stability analysis of space-time Galerkin methods with isogeometric approach.
result: They show that condition numbers can grow exponentially even for Fredholm symbols, and that stability of the space-time IgA methods relates to conditioning of block Toeplitz-like matrices.
conclusion: The paper provides theoretical insights into conditioning and stability, with specific examples and numerical experiments, and lists open problems.

title: Quadratic Optimization Over Probability Measures With Coupling Constraints
authors: Yong Sheng Soh Hoang Anh Tran
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider solving an optimization instance in which the objective is quadratic and where the decision variable is a probability measure. Our class of problems are motivated by applications arising from optimal transport (with the Gromov-Wasserstein problem being a prominent example) as well as energy landscape minimization. Because the objective depends quadratically on the decision variable, our class of problems fall outside the standard modeling framework of the Generalized Moment Problems (which requires the objective to be linear). To this end, we propose a hierarchy of convex relaxations based on searching over probability measures over products of the base space. These have a natural interpretation with the moment Sum-of-squares hierarchy-a prominent framework for solving polynomial optimization instances, which we adapt to accommodate probability measures. A key conceptual contribution is to introduce a notion of positive-semidefiniteness that extends the usual notion over matrices. Under the assumption that the decision variables satisfy certain marginal constraints (as in the Kantorovich formulation of the optimal transport problem), we establish convergence of our hierarchy towards the globally optimal solution. Under the additional assumption that the objective is a polynomial, we propose a moment-SOS type hierarchy of finite dimensional semidefinite programs whose optimal solution converges to that of the original quadratic optimization over measures. We demonstrate our framework with numerical experiments. More generally, optimization over measures where the objective and/or constraint depends on the decision in a polynomial way is a fundamental problem. It is hoped that our work provides a road-map as to how the ideas of the SOS-ordinarily developed for polynomial optimization-may be applied to a broader class of non-linear problems involving measures.
tldr: This paper proposes a hierarchy of convex relaxations for quadratic optimization over probability measures with coupling constraints, establishing convergence and a moment-SOS type SDP hierarchy.
motivation: Quadratic optimization over probability measures arises in optimal transport and energy landscape minimization, but it does not fit the linear framework of Generalized Moment Problems.
method: They introduce a hierarchy of convex relaxations based on probability measures over products of the base space, generalize positive semidefiniteness to measures, and adapt the moment-SOS hierarchy for polynomial objectives.
result: Under marginal constraints, the hierarchy converges to the global optimum; for polynomial objectives, finite-dimensional semidefinite programs yield convergent approximations.
conclusion: The work extends SOS techniques to non-linear problems involving measures, providing a roadmap for applying polynomial optimization ideas to broader classes of problems.

title: Eigenvalue Bounds For Preconditioned Symmetric Multiple Saddle-point Matrices With Block-triangular Preconditioners
authors: Luca Bergamaschi, Michele Bergamaschi, John W. Pearson
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop eigenvalue bounds for symmetric, block-tridiagonal multiple saddle-point linear systems, preconditioned with block-triangular matrices, based on approximate Schur complements. Irrespective on the number of blocks, we prove that all complex eigenvalues, with nontrivial imaginary part, are strictly contained in a circle within the complex plane, with center 1. The real and positive eigenvalues are bounded in terms of the extremal roots of a sequences of parametric polynomials. Numerical results reveal that the bounds describe very well the eigenvalue distribution of the preconditioned matrix.
tldr: This paper derives eigenvalue bounds for preconditioned symmetric multiple saddle-point matrices, proving that complex eigenvalues lie in a circle centered at 1 and bounding real eigenvalues via parametric polynomials.
motivation: To improve the convergence of iterative solvers for large-scale saddle-point systems by analyzing the eigenvalue distribution of preconditioned matrices, which is crucial for practical computational efficiency.
method: Mathematical analysis of block-triangular preconditioners based on approximate Schur complements, yielding rigorous bounds for complex and real eigenvalues, supplemented by numerical experiments.
result: The bounds are tight and accurately describe the eigenvalue distribution of the preconditioned matrix, irrespective of the number of blocks.
conclusion: The theoretical bounds provide a framework for designing and evaluating block-triangular preconditioners for multiple saddle-point systems, benefiting numerical linear algebra applications.

title: Compressive Sensing - Introduction And Relations To Deep Learning
authors: Hung-Hsu Chou, Johannes Maly, Holger Rauhut
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compressive sensing predicts that sparse vectors (signals) can be recovered from a small number of linear measurements via efficient algorithms. This finding, which dates back two decades, has triggered a paradigm shift in signal processing and initiated many developments both in practical signal-processing applications, such as medical imaging, radar, and astronomy, and on the theoretical side. More recently, seminal connections to the field of deep learning have led to further advances in the field, such as the use of unrolled neural networks for sparse recovery and the discovery that common training algorithms (variants of gradient descent) favor sparsity in overparameterized scenarios -- the so-called implicit bias phenomenon. This article gives an introduction to compressive sensing and outlines connections to deep learning. In particular, we will discuss generalization for neural networks generated by unrolling sparse recovery algorithms and implicit regularization for gradient descent applied to learning simplified linear neural networks.
tldr: A review article introducing compressive sensing and its connections to deep learning, including unrolled networks and implicit bias.
motivation: To provide an accessible introduction to compressive sensing and highlight recent intersections with deep learning.
method: The article reviews classical compressive sensing theory and then discusses how deep learning techniques, such as unrolled networks and implicit regularization, relate to sparse recovery.
result: Discusses generalization guarantees for unrolled networks and implicit bias phenomena for gradient descent in linear neural networks.
conclusion: Compressive sensing and deep learning are increasingly intertwined, with deep learning offering new algorithms and theoretical insights.

title: A High-Accuracy Numerical Homogenization Framework For Quasiperiodic Hamilton--Jacobi Equations
authors: Kai Jiang, Meng Li, Juan Zhang, Lei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop an accurate numerical homogenization framework for computing effective Hamiltonians of quasiperiodic Hamilton--Jacobi equations (QHJEs) with convex Hamiltonians of the form [MATH], where [MATH] is quasiperiodic. Computing effective Hamiltonians in the quasiperiodic setting requires solving QHJEs posed on the whole space. Their solutions generally possess neither translational symmetry nor decay and may exhibit low regularity. These features pose substantial challenges for numerical computation. To address these difficulties, we introduce a quasiperiodic boundary condition, which allows the original whole-space problem to be treated on a bounded domain while preserving quasiperiodicity at the boundary. We then propose an SL--FPR scheme that combines a semi-Lagrangian approximation with the finite points recovery method and establish stability and error estimates for the resulting scheme. We also extend the quasiperiodic homogenization result from the quadratic case to general [MATH] and apply the proposed method to accurately approximate the corresponding effective Hamiltonians. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence and applicability of the method and validate the extended homogenization results.
tldr: A numerical homogenization framework is developed for quasiperiodic Hamilton-Jacobi equations, using a quasiperiodic boundary condition and an SL-FPR scheme.
motivation: Computing effective Hamiltonians for quasiperiodic HJ equations is challenging because solutions lack symmetry and decay, and may have low regularity.
method: The method introduces a quasiperiodic boundary condition to handle the whole-space problem on a bounded domain, and uses a semi-Lagrangian approximation with finite points recovery (SL-FPR) scheme.
result: Stability and error estimates are established, homogenization results are extended to general convex Hamiltonians, and numerical experiments confirm convergence.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides an accurate and convergent approach for approximating effective Hamiltonians in quasiperiodic settings.

title: Universal Random Coding For Successive Refinement Of Individual Sequences Based On Lempel-Ziv Complexity
authors: Neri Merhav
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work extends an earlier proposed universal random-coding ensemble for sample-wise lossy compression of individual sequences to the two-stage (successive-refinement) setting --- an extension that is not quite straightforward, as explained in the sequel. The construction has three layers. First, a complete, self-contained direct/converse match in the language of type classes and typical sequences, a two-stage analogue of Rimoldi's classical characterization (applied in the superalphabet of blocks). Second, a realization of the same rates via a random-coding scheme built from the Lempel--Ziv (LZ78) complexity rather than the type-class uniform measure the first layer relies on, since an LZ-based ensemble is universal across source statistics and distortion measures, carries no block-length parameter in the codebook itself, and is directly implementable. Third, we give a fully type-free achievability construction (no joint types of [MATH]-vectors appear anywhere in its search criterion) and show it matches the same converse exactly, reaching every point of the achievable region: the same converse from the first layer already binds any code, type-free schemes included, so no separate argument is needed to certify the match. We also describe (without proof) how to extend the type-free construction to any fixed number [MATH] of stages. Finally, we show this paper's achievable region is a superset of the one obtained by a companion paper, which is based on a finite-state modeling approach to a similar two-stage problem, extending a known single-stage domination result to two stages.
tldr: This paper extends universal random coding for lossy compression of individual sequences to the successive refinement setting using Lempel-Ziv complexity.
motivation: To generalize the random-coding ensemble to two-stage (successive refinement) lossy compression, achieving rate-distortion tradeoffs for individual sequences without assuming a source model.
method: The construction has three layers: first a type-class based direct/converse match, then a realization using LZ78 complexity for universality, and finally a fully type-free achievability construction; also extends to more stages.
result: It reaches every point of the achievable region and shows it is a superset of a companion paper's region based on finite-state modeling.
conclusion: The paper provides a universal, implementable coding scheme for successive refinement with a type-free construction.

title: A Scenario-Based Evaluation Of Crqc+ai Vulnerability Spectrum For Tls 1.3 Cryptographic Dependencies
authors: Noel Grover, Mussie Haile, Brad Pedersen, Eric Uner, Bradley J Erickson
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper evaluates quantum and AI-accelerated risks to TLS 1.3 cryptographic dependencies under an evidence-tiered model, distinguishing mechanism-backed threats (Shor algorithm against RSA and ECC) from contingency-backed risks to lattice-based post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and hypothesis-only risks to hash-based and symmetric primitives. We do not identify any known breaks of ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, or AES-256. Instead, we use explicit scenario assumptions, organized as a four-scenario capability model with parameters and pseudocode for reproducibility, to stress-test migration timelines accompanied by parameter sensitivity analysis and explicit falsification analysis. The primary methodological contribution is a reproducible scenario-estimation instrument together with its explicit update mechanics: every parameter is a named, anchored quantity that can be varied and the model rerun; a stated protocol maps observed conformance to, or deviation from, the modeled curves onto revisions of specific parameters, so progressive refinements can be tested against accumulating historical data. The paper is a methodological companion to quantum resource-estimation studies and to expert-elicitation timeline surveys such as the Global Risk Institute quantum threat reports, with its revision rules stated explicitly. As of mid-2026, the model does not show any NIST-approved algorithms as broken. Instead, the vulnerability spectrum under different scenarios shows RSA risk crossing the 50% threshold between 2030-2032 and the PQC risk becoming a non-zero risk after 2032-2035 under contingency scenarios conditional on the unproven dimension-collapse. We urge PQC migration as mandatory per the 2030 and 2031 federal deadlines and by Mosca HNDL reasoning, and that crypto-agility and hybrid cryptographic deployment be considered necessary complements to any PQC migration efforts.
tldr: This paper presents a scenario-based evaluation framework for assessing quantum and AI risks to TLS 1.3 cryptographic dependencies, proposing specific migration timelines and a reproducible estimation instrument.
motivation: To provide a reproducible, evidence-tiered assessment of quantum threats to TLS 1.3 to guide migration decisions, addressing uncertainty in quantum risk timelines.
method: Defines a four-scenario capability model with explicit parameters and pseudocode, distinguishes mechanism-backed, contingency-backed, and hypothesis-only risks, and incorporates parameter sensitivity and falsification analysis.
result: Indicates that RSA risk crosses the 50% threshold between 2030-2032 and PQC risk becomes non-zero after 2032-2035 under contingency scenarios, while no NIST-approved algorithms are broken as of mid-2026.
conclusion: Urges mandatory PQC migration by 2030/2031 federal deadlines and emphasizes crypto-agility and hybrid cryptographic deployment as necessary complements.

title: Exact Cvp Is NP-Complete For Principal Cyclotomic Ideals
authors: Jiaqi Liu, Yansong Feng, Yanbin Pan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that exact Euclidean decision-CVP is [MATH]-complete on coefficient lattices of nonzero principal ideals in the power-of-two cyclotomic rings [MATH]. A deterministic reduction from X3C produces an integral target and squared threshold [MATH] such that the closest squared distance is exactly [MATH] in YES instances and at least [MATH] in NO instances. The ideal elements within squared distance [MATH] are in bijection with exact covers, which also gives [MATH]-hardness of exact search-CVP under polynomial-time Turing reductions. We further lift these instances to full-rank principal ideals of [MATH], where [MATH]. The lift preserves principality, doubles the dimension, and scales corresponding squared distances by eight. Hence exact decision-CVP is [MATH]-complete and exact search-CVP is [MATH]-hard on principal cyclic ideal lattices. Both results admit uniformly computable fixed-family forms: for each X3C universe size, the principal cyclotomic and cyclic ideals can be fixed before the triple collection is known, with only the targets and thresholds depending on the collection. motivation: To establish hardness of lattice problems in specific algebraic structures, relevant to cryptanalysis and post-quantum security.
method: Provides a deterministic reduction from the exact cover by 3-sets (X3C) problem to decision-CVP on coefficient lattices of principal ideals, and lifts to full-rank cyclic ideals.
result: Shows exact decision-CVP is NP-complete and search-CVP is NP-hard on principal cyclotomic and cyclic lattices, with uniform fixed-family forms.
conclusion: Resolves open questions about the complexity of exact CVP on cyclic lattices, confirming worst-case hardness.

title: NeuronGuard: Robust Llm Safety Alignment Via Ablation-Aware Safety Signal Redistribution
authors: Anjun Gao, Yueyang Quan, Yufei Xia, Zhuqing Liu, Minghong Fang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety alignment in large language models (LLMs) remains brittle against a growing spectrum of attacks. Jailbreak attacks bypass safety mechanisms through crafted prompts, while neuron-level attacks directly prune safety-critical neurons post-deployment. Both exploit a common weakness: safety-relevant information concentrates in a sparse neuron subset. We present NeuronGuard, a fine-tuning-stage defense that simultaneously hardens LLMs against both attack classes by redistributing safety signals across a broader set of neurons. NeuronGuard dynamically identifies safety-critical neurons via periodically refreshed per-layer linear classifiers, forces refusal behavior under deliberate neuron ablation, and applies KL-divergence regularization for distributional consistency. A randomized gradient projection strategy preserves downstream task utility by resolving conflicts between the defense and task objectives. We provide a formal guarantee that NeuronGuard strictly reduces the attack success rate (ASR) upper bound, and experiments across three LLMs, six state-of-the-art attack strategies, and multimodal settings confirm near-zero ASR while maintaining task accuracy, including against white-box adaptive adversaries.
tldr: NeuronGuard is a fine-tuning defense that redistributes safety signals across neurons in LLMs to resist both jailbreak and neuron-level attacks.
motivation: LLM safety alignment is fragile against a spectrum of attacks, and safety information concentrated in a sparse neuron subset can be exploited or pruned.
method: NeuronGuard dynamically identifies safety-critical neurons via per-layer linear classifiers, enforces refusal behavior under ablation, applies KL-divergence regularization, and uses randomized gradient projection to preserve task utility.
result: Experiments across three LLMs and six attack strategies show near-zero attack success rate with maintained task accuracy, including against adaptive adversaries.
conclusion: The method provides a formal guarantee of reduced attack success rate upper bound and effectively hardens LLMs against both jailbreak and neuron-level attacks.

title: Optimal Rank Lotteries For Truthful Unit-Interval Covering
authors: Alexandros A. Voudouris
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In truthful interval covering, each agent has a private interval of unit length, and the goal is to decide where to place a public unit interval so as to minimize the total uncovered length while incentivizing the agents to be truthful. Previous work proposed a universally strategyproof lottery over order-statistic mechanisms with approximation ratio at most [MATH], and established a lower bound of [MATH] for this class of mechanisms. We close this gap by characterizing the approximation ratio of every report-independent lottery over order-statistics. In particular, we show that, for every [MATH], the optimal approximation ratio for this class is [MATH]. Beyond rank lotteries, we show that every universally strategyproof randomized mechanism has approximation ratio at least [MATH].
