motivation: The authors aim to characterize the box dimension of graphs of certain trigonometric series and to resolve a question about when the associated chirp functional vanishes at rational points.
method: They use Fourier analysis and arithmetic properties of the chirp functional, along with a resolution theorem for trigonometric polynomials, to establish lower bounds on the box dimension.
result: They prove that for any nonconstant real trigonometric polynomial, the chirp functional cannot vanish at all rationals, implying a strictly positive dimension for certain functions and distinguishing structural vanishing from arithmetic vanishing.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into the fractal geometry of Riemann-type functions and highlights connections to modular elliptic curves and the Prime Number Theorem.

title: One Burst Of t-Deletion And One Burst Of t-Substitution Error-Correcting Codes
authors: Yajuan Liu, Han Cai, Tolga M. Duman
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synchronization errors, including insertions, deletions, and substitutions, may occur in bursts in communication systems such as DNA data storage, file synchronization, and magnetic recording. In this paper, we study an error model con?sisting of one burst of t-deletions and one burst of t-substitutions. By reformulating the original sequence into a matrix form, we propose an explicit construction of error-correcting codes capable of correcting one burst of t-deletions and one burst of t-substitutions with O(log n) redundancy.
tldr: This paper proposes an explicit construction of error-correcting codes that correct one burst of t-deletions and one burst of t-substitutions with logarithmic redundancy.
motivation: Synchronization errors like deletions and substitutions can occur in bursts in communication systems such as DNA data storage, file synchronization, and magnetic recording, motivating the study of codes that correct such burst errors.
method: By reformulating the original sequence into a matrix form, the authors propose an explicit construction of error-correcting codes that can correct one burst of t-deletions and one burst of t-substitutions.
result: The construction achieves O(log n) redundancy, which is order-optimal.
conclusion: The paper provides a new code construction with efficient redundancy for correcting bursts of deletion and substitution errors, contributing to classical error correction for synchronization errors.

title: Samplet Compression For Conditionally Positive Definite Kernels And Universal Kriging
authors: Sara Avesani, R\"udiger Kempf, Michael Multerer, Holger Wendland
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a samplet-based framework for the efficient numerical solution of saddle-point systems arising from conditionally positive definite (CPD) kernel approximation in general and universal Kriging in particular. The vanishing moment property of samplets as well as the particular structure of the associated scaling distributions, which correspond to discrete orthogonal polynomials, allow for a numerically favorable representation of these saddle-point systems. Concretely, they enable a natural null-space reduction of the indefinite saddle-point system to a (large) linear system for the detail coefficients and a small triangular system for the polynomial coefficients. We derive error bounds for the approximation by polyharmonic splines in Beppo-Levi spaces and show that the detail coefficients span precisely the subspace on which the CPD kernel is positive definite, rendering the reduced block symmetric positive definite. In view of the quasi-sparsity of the samplet-transformed kernel matrix for asymptotically smooth kernels, the resulting method achieves O(N log N) cost for the assembly and the storage of the saddle-point system. The reduced system can efficiently be solved by a sparse Cholesky factorization. We illustrate the framework with three applications, namely Gaussian process regression with generalized covariances, landmark-based image registration via samplet-compressed thin plate splines, and three-dimensional mesh deformation.
tldr: This paper presents a samplet-based framework for efficient numerical solution of saddle-point systems in conditionally positive definite kernel approximation and universal Kriging.
motivation: To address the computational challenges of large-scale kernel approximation and Kriging, which involve expensive saddle-point systems.
method: The method uses samplets with vanishing moments to reduce the indefinite saddle-point system to a smaller symmetric positive definite system, enabling quasi-sparse representation and O(N log N) assembly.
result: The reduced system can be solved efficiently via sparse Cholesky factorization, and the framework is demonstrated on Gaussian process regression, image registration, and mesh deformation.
conclusion: The samplet-based approach provides a numerically favorable and scalable solution for CPD kernel approximation and universal Kriging problems.

title: Arithmetic Conditions For Julia Sets To Have Positive Area
authors: Hongyu Qu Jianyong Qiao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, for quadratic polynomials with Cremer points or Siegel disks whose boundaries don't contain critical points, we give an arithmetic condition for their Julia sets to have positive area. Our proof relies on the Siegel Return Machinery as well as the pseudo-Siegel disk theory developed by Dudko and Lyubich.
tldr: The paper provides an arithmetic condition for Julia sets of quadratic polynomials with Cremer points or Siegel disks to have positive area, using advanced dynamical systems machinery.
motivation: Understanding when Julia sets have positive area is a fundamental problem in complex dynamics, and this work addresses it for a specific class of polynomials.
method: The proof employs the Siegel Return Machinery and pseudo-Siegel disk theory developed by Dudko and Lyubich.
result: They establish an arithmetic condition under which the Julia set of such polynomials has positive area.
conclusion: This contributes to the classification of Julia sets with positive area for quadratic polynomials with neutral periodic points.

title: Wave Selection At An $O(2)$-Hopf Bifurcation In Conservative Two-Component Pde Systems
authors: Saadet S. \"ozer, Taylan \c{s}eng\"ul, Burhan Tiryakioglu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At an [MATH]-equivariant Hopf bifurcation a spatially periodic system selects between traveling waves and standing waves, and which branch appears and whether it is stable is decided by two cubic normal form coefficients. Obtaining these coefficients for a given PDE has required a derivation carried out afresh for each model. We remove that step for two-component systems with conservative polynomial differential nonlinearities on a one-dimensional periodic domain, deriving closed form formulas for both coefficients. They are expressed directly in terms of the array of nonlinear PDE coefficients and the spectral data of the linearization, its critical eigenvectors, adjoint eigenvectors, and non-critical resolvents. We give verifiable conditions under which the underlying center manifold reduction is valid: a structural condition on the principal part of the linearization that yields the required resolvent estimate, and a condition on the Fourier symbol that we show is equivalent to the required spectral gap. In contrast to the model specific computations available previously, the resulting formulas apply to any system in the class without further derivation. A companion implementation evaluates the two normal form coefficients from the coefficient array and verifies the assumptions for a given system. We specialize the formulas to two applications: a strain-gradient regularization of the nonlinear [MATH]-system, whose quadratic case contains a previously studied model as a special case, and a first order conservative bilinear family, not previously analyzed, in which every bifurcation scenario allowed by the general classification is realized.
tldr: This paper derives closed-form formulas for cubic normal form coefficients in O(2)-Hopf bifurcations for a class of conservative two-component PDEs, removing the need for model-specific derivations.
motivation: The authors aim to generalize the computation of these coefficients, which previously required individual derivations for each PDE model, to a broader class of systems.
method: They derive the formulas directly from the PDE's nonlinear coefficients and linearized spectral data, and provide verifiable conditions for the center manifold reduction.
result: Closed-form expressions for both cubic normal form coefficients are obtained, applicable to any system in the class, with a companion implementation and applications to two specific families.
conclusion: The work simplifies bifurcation analysis for two-component conservative PDEs and demonstrates that all bifurcation scenarios of the general classification can be realized in a first-order bilinear family.

title: Mean Field Game Model For Human Capital Accumulation Under Budget Constraints
authors: Saeed Sadeghi Arjmand
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a deterministic first-order mean field game model for human capital accumulation in which a continuum of agents invest in education and training to reach a certain qualification level in minimum time. The productivity of learning depends on both the individual's current level of human capital and the distribution of the population, modeling knowledge spillovers and social interactions. Learning is financed by the income generated by existing human capital, leading to a state constraint requiring the financial resources to remain nonnegative throughout the evolution. For a fixed population flow, we formulate the individual problem as a state-constrained minimum-time optimal control problem with time-dependent dynamics. We establish the existence of optimal controls and trajectories, analyze the associated value function through the Dynamic Programming Principle and a Hamilton--Jacobi equation, and characterize the optimal learning effort under suitable regularity and convexity assumptions. The optimal feedback induces a continuity equation describing the evolution of the population distribution. The resulting mean field game is formulated as a fixed-point problem for the population flow. By constructing a compact invariant set and applying Schauder's fixed-point theorem, we prove the existence of at least one equilibrium on every finite population horizon, while the individual minimum-time problem remains formulated on the infinite time horizon.
tldr: This paper analyzes a mean field game model for human capital accumulation under budget constraints, proving existence of equilibria via optimal control and fixed-point methods.
motivation: The authors aim to model how a continuum of agents optimally invest in education, considering knowledge spillovers and financial constraints, and to prove the existence of equilibrium in such a setting.
method: They formulate the individual's problem as a state-constrained minimum-time optimal control problem, derive a Hamilton-Jacobi equation, and then use Schauder's fixed-point theorem on a compact invariant set to prove existence of a mean field equilibrium.
result: Existence of optimal controls and trajectories is established, and at least one equilibrium is shown to exist on any finite population horizon, with the individual problem on an infinite time horizon.
conclusion: The paper provides a rigorous theoretical foundation for a mean field game of human capital accumulation, but it is entirely unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information and related fields.

title: Centers Of Quantum Schur Superalgebras From Hecke Algebras
authors: Qiang Fu, Yingshan Luo, Chengquan Sun
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the center of the quantum Schur superalgebra [MATH] associated with the general linear Lie superalgebra [MATH]. Using the super Schur--Weyl duality due to Mitsuhashi between the quantum supergroup [MATH] and the Hecke algebra [MATH], we transfer two known bases of the center of [MATH], namely the Geck--Rouquier basis and the Jones basis, to the center of [MATH]. This yields two distinct bases for [MATH], indexed respectively by the symmetrized hook set [MATH] and by the full [MATH]-hook set [MATH]. Our approach relies on a detailed analysis of the ring [MATH] of doubly symmetric polynomials satisfying [MATH] independent of [MATH], and of its power-sum bases.
tldr: The paper constructs explicit bases for the center of quantum Schur superalgebras via super Schur-Weyl duality from Hecke algebra centers.
motivation: To study the center of quantum Schur superalgebras, which is a fundamental object in representation theory and quantum groups.
method: Uses super Schur-Weyl duality to transfer known bases (Geck-Rouquier and Jones) from the Hecke algebra center to the quantum Schur superalgebra center, relying on doubly symmetric polynomials.
result: Obtains two distinct bases for the center, indexed by symmetrized hook sets and full hook sets.
conclusion: Provides a detailed algebraic description of the centers, contributing to the structure theory of quantum superalgebras.

title: TrustShiftProbe: Characterizing, Benchmarking, And Defending Staged Trust Attacks On Mcp Servers
authors: Mehrdad Rostamzadeh, Sidhant Narula, Mohammad Ghasemigol, Daniel Takabi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has emerged as the standard layer connecting Large Language Model agents to external tool backends. This openness introduces a severe server-side threat we term TrustShift: a compromised MCP server behaves benignly during an initial conditioning phase, building operational reliance and suppressing agent skepticism, before switching to an adversarial payload once an interaction threshold is reached. The evasion is temporal, not syntactic: benign at deploy time, the server's defection is invisible to predeployment static analysis, which sees only the honest phase. Switched payloads range from overt structural violations to schema-valid manipulations, the latter preserving outer protocol compliance to evade runtime middleware filters. Crucially, TrustShift originates in the server-controlled tool channel, not user prompts (unlike indirect prompt injection) or the transport (unlike man-in-the-middle): the adversary is the trusted server endpoint itself. We introduce TrustShiftProbe, an evaluation and defense framework with four contributions: (1) a stateful temporal threat model of the agent-server lifecycle as a benign conditioning phase followed by an adversarial defection at a trust horizon; (2) a language-agnostic attack engine that instantiates each variant as a compromised MCP server across four production domains; (3) SHIELD, a multi-tier, zero-oracle runtime defense at the MCP transport boundary that audits server payloads against behavioral baselines learned during clean trust windows; and (4) a taxonomy of nine TrustShift variants spanning three execution mechanisms (structural violation, semantic corruption, scope expansion) and three adversarial objectives (disruption, exfiltration, and their combination). Across frontier proprietary and open-weight models, TrustShift attacks achieve a 69.5% mean attack success rate that SHIELD mitigates to 42.7%.
tldr: Introduces TrustShiftProbe, a framework for characterizing and defending against staged trust attacks on Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
motivation: MCP servers are vulnerable to temporal evasion attacks where a compromised server initially behaves benignly to build trust, then switches to adversarial payloads, bypassing static and runtime defenses.
method: Proposes a threat model with benign conditioning and adversarial defection, an attack engine instantiating nine TrustShift variants, and SHIELD, a multi-tier runtime defense that audits server payloads against behavioral baselines.
result: TrustShift attacks achieve a 69.5% mean attack success rate, which SHIELD mitigates to 42.7% across frontier models.
conclusion: TrustShift attacks represent a significant security threat to MCP-based agents, and SHIELD offers an effective defense, though further enhancement is needed.

title: A Unified Dynamical Modeling Framework For Cruise Control And Adaptive Cruise Control
authors: Shian Wang Mingfeng Shang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive cruise control (ACC) vehicles are the first generation of automated vehicles. While fully automated vehicles are expected to benefit traffic flow, field experiments have shown that commercially available ACC vehicles may instead degrade it by reducing string stability and roadway throughput. To mitigate these effects, existing studies adjust the ACC control algorithm or introduce additional control inputs; however, few have examined the transition between the cruise control (CC) and ACC modes without modifying the ACC control algorithm itself, leaving the impacts of ACC vehicles incompletely understood. To address this gap, we propose a unified dynamical model of CC and ACC that interpolates continuously between the two modes through a sigmoid weighting function, and improve traffic flow by designing the mode switching. Based on this new model, we conduct an equilibrium and string stability analysis of the platoon, revealing the trade-off among safety, throughput, and string stability. The optimal switching threshold is designed under throughput-priority and safety-priority criteria, and compared against the threshold adopted by commercially available ACC vehicles. Numerical experiments show that, with a properly designed switching threshold, the throughput increases by up to 58.6% and the average speed variation, a measure of speed oscillations, decreases by up to 39.7% relative to the commercial baseline. We conclude that the excessively large switching threshold of commercially available ACC vehicles is a likely cause of their negative impact on traffic flow, and that this impact can be mitigated by properly reducing the threshold toward a safer and more string-stable regime.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified dynamical model of cruise control and adaptive cruise control that interpolates between modes using a sigmoid weighting function, and shows that optimizing the switching threshold can improve traffic throughput and string stability.
motivation: Existing ACC vehicles may degrade traffic flow by reducing string stability and throughput. The authors aim to understand and mitigate these effects by examining the mode transition between CC and ACC without modifying the ACC control algorithm itself.
method: They develop a unified model that continuously interpolates between CC and ACC using a sigmoid weighting function, and perform equilibrium and string stability analysis of a platoon. They design optimal switching thresholds under throughput-priority and safety-priority criteria.
result: Numerical experiments show that with a properly designed switching threshold, throughput increases by up to 58.6% and speed oscillations decrease by up to 39.7% relative to commercial baselines.
conclusion: The excessively large switching threshold of commercial ACC vehicles is a likely cause of their negative impact on traffic flow, and this can be mitigated by reducing the threshold toward a safer and more string-stable regime.

title: Beyond The Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis Of The Agent Payments Protocol (ap2)
authors: Avital Aviv, Parth A. Gandh, Ron Bitton, Asaf Shabtai
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), introduced by Google, enables large language model (LLM)-driven shopping agents to authorize and execute payments on behalf of users. Its signed Checkout and Payment Mandates protect the integrity of transaction data after signing. Agent interactions and external inputs that shape a transaction before authorization remain outside that protection, including Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A2A) messages and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls. Prior work identified replay and prompt-injection attacks in AP2 v0.1. AP2 v0.2 addresses some of these issues but adds capabilities and deployment assumptions that require renewed analysis. We present a systematic security analysis of AP2 v0.2 based on its roles, transaction lifecycle, deployment architectures, and trust boundaries. We divide the lifecycle into five phases and identify five deployment architectures. Using MAESTRO (Multi-Agent Environment, Security, Threat, Risk, Outcome), we model four threat actors, eleven attack surfaces, eighteen adversary capabilities, and six attacker goals. The resulting catalog contains 48 threats spanning five attack families. We score these threats with the Artificial Intelligence Vulnerability Scoring System (AIVSS), identifying eight that reach the High band in at least one architecture. Because no complete public AP2 deployment was available, we build a testbed spanning all five architectures and develop five proof-of-concept demonstrations covering all eight High-risk threats and their mitigations. We also develop a deployment-aware scanner that maps applicable threats to static, cross-role consistency, and adversarial checks. Our analysis shows that valid mandate signatures alone do not ensure that an agent-mediated transaction reflects the user's intent when its pre-authorization context is manipulated.
tldr: This paper presents a systematic security analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) for LLM-driven shopping agents, identifying 48 threats and demonstrating that valid mandate signatures do not ensure user intent.
motivation: To analyze security of AP2 v0.2, which handles payments for LLM-driven agents, given prior attacks and new deployment assumptions.
method: Used MAESTRO threat modeling to map attack surfaces, adversary capabilities, and goals; built a testbed covering five architectures and developed proof-of-concept demonstrations for eight High-risk threats.
result: Identified 48 threats across five families, with eight reaching High severity; demonstrated attacks exploiting pre-authorization context manipulation.
conclusion: Valid mandate signatures alone are insufficient; the pre-authorization context must be protected to ensure transaction reflects user intent.

title: Stain-fl: Stealthy Targeted Attack Injection With Contextual Triggers In Federated Learning
authors: Ashlinder Kaur, Purnima Murali Mohan, Zengxiang Li, Tram Truong-Huu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated video anomaly detection trains model collaboratively without sharing raw surveillance footage, but limited server-side visibility lets compromised clients to inject backdoor via malicious updates. This paper introduces STAIN-FL, a stealthy targeted backdoor attack injection framework that uses naturally occurring surveillance conditions, including low-light scenes, indoor settings, and crowd density, as contextual triggers. STAIN-FL combines anomaly-to-benign label with gradient masking over least-updated coordinates to preserve clean accuracy while inducing trigger-conditioned misclassification. We evaluate STAIN-FL on using 1024-dimensional I3D features in a non-IID four-client multi-agency setting, comparing FedAvg and FedProx under sparse and continuous attacks. Results show that sparse attacks have low-detectability, operationally significant attacks rather than high-intensity attacks: they keep the mean clean-accuracy drop below [MATH], yet still misclassify more than half of triggered anomalies at peak backdoor accuracy under FedAvg ([MATH]) and FedProx ([MATH]). Under FedAvg, the sparse backdoor remains above the [MATH] backdoor-accuracy threshold for an average of [MATH] post-attack rounds, highlighting the persistence risk of contextually triggered attacks in surveillance systems.
tldr: Introduces STAIN-FL, a stealthy backdoor attack framework for federated video anomaly detection that uses contextual triggers like low-light and crowd density to misclassify anomalies while preserving clean accuracy.
motivation: Federated video anomaly detection is vulnerable to backdoor attacks from compromised clients, but existing attacks are detectable or lack stealth; the authors aim to create a realistic, low-detectability attack using natural surveillance conditions.
method: STAIN-FL combines anomaly-to-benign label mapping with gradient masking over least-updated coordinates to preserve clean accuracy while inducing trigger-conditioned misclassification; it is evaluated using I3D features in a non-IID four-client setup with FedAvg and FedProx.
result: Sparse attacks show low detectability, maintaining clean accuracy drops below a threshold while misclassifying over half of triggered anomalies at peak backdoor accuracy under FedAvg and FedProx; the backdoor persists for many post-attack rounds.
conclusion: Contextually triggered attacks pose a persistent risk in federated surveillance systems, highlighting the need for robust defenses against such stealthy backdoor injections.

title: RAGSentinel: Certifiable Geometric Consensus For Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Yueyang Quan, Anjun Gao, Yufei Xia, Minghong Fang, Zhuqing Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves the factuality of large language models by grounding responses in external documents, but it also exposes a critical security vulnerability: adversarial documents injected into the knowledge database can enter the context window and steer the model toward targeted incorrect answers. Existing post-retrieval defenses rely on instruction following, parametric knowledge, or text-level consistency, all of which can be imitated or optimized against by adaptive attackers. We propose RAGSentinel, a training-free, label-free defense for black-box RAG systems. RAGSentinel uses a surrogate encoder to measure query-conditioned hidden-state shifts induced by retrieved documents, removes shared topic directions, and filters poisoned documents as geometric outliers from a robust majority consensus. We prove that, under an honest-majority assumption and a representation-level separation condition, RAGSentinel exactly recovers a poison-free majority-sized context. Experiments across three question-answering datasets, three LLM families, and multiple poisoning attacks show that RAGSentinel consistently achieves low attack success rates while preserving competitive accuracy and remaining effective against adaptive attacks with full pipeline knowledge.
tldr: RAGSentinel is a training-free, label-free defense that filters poisoned documents in retrieval-augmented generation using geometric consensus on query-conditioned hidden-state shifts.
motivation: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is vulnerable to adversarial document injection, and existing defenses are insufficient against adaptive attackers.
method: RAGSentinel uses a surrogate encoder to measure query-conditioned hidden-state shifts, removes shared topic directions, and filters poisoned documents as geometric outliers via robust majority consensus, with a provable recovery guarantee under honest-majority assumptions.
result: Experiments across three QA datasets, three LLM families, and multiple poisoning attacks show low attack success rates, competitive accuracy, and robustness against adaptive attacks.
conclusion: RAGSentinel provides a certifiable and effective defense against poisoning attacks in black-box RAG systems without requiring training or labels.

title: What Guides The Agent? Adjudicating Unauthorized Behavior Via Localizing Behavior-Guiding Instructions
authors: Yichao Gao, Yumo Zhang, Yunhao Yao, Haohua Du, Puhan Luo, Ruiqi Li, Zhiqiang Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents integrated with external resources gain complex task capabilities, yet the unified natural-language context channel makes them vulnerable to injection attacks: untrusted external data may be dynamically parsed as behavior-guiding instructions during LLM inference, thereby subverting the agent's decision. Existing defenses focus on static detection or isolation of malicious content at the input/output level, remains insufficient for detecting such dynamic inducements that arise during model reasoning. We propose Attnlocate, a runtime framework for fine-grained localization of context spans that genuinely influence tool-calling decisions, i.e., behavior-guiding instructions. Attnlocate casts this localization problem as an object detection task, aiming to detect the distinctive activation traces induced by behavior-guiding instructions within the attention matrix. Specifically, we design a multi-head, multi-layer attention aggregation scheme to construct a token-level feature space tailored for object detection. Then, a 1-D U-Net equipped with an anchor-free detection head is deployed to detect these spans. Finally, based on the authority of the provider from which the detected behavior-guiding spans originate, Attnlocate dynamically adjudicates malicious invocation attempts. We evaluate Attnlocate across ten agent configurations from five LLM families, covering scenarios involving indirect prompt injection and tool poisoning. Attnlocate achieves a mean IoU of 0.743, an average AUROC of 0.956, and a 0.934 true-positive rate at 0.067 false-positive rate. It also transfers effectively across unseen models and supports authority policy adaptation without retraining.
tldr: This paper proposes Attnlocate, a runtime framework to localize behavior-guiding instructions in the attention matrix of LLM agents to detect and adjudicate injection attacks.
motivation: LLM agents are vulnerable to injection attacks where external data is parsed as instructions during inference, and existing defenses are insufficient for dynamic inducements arising during reasoning.
method: Attnlocate frames localization as object detection, using a multi-head, multi-layer attention aggregation to construct token-level features, and a 1-D U-Net with an anchor-free head to detect spans; it then adjudicates based on the authority of the detected span's source.
result: Evaluated on ten agent configurations from five LLM families, Attnlocate achieves a mean IoU of 0.743, average AUROC of 0.956, and a true-positive rate of 0.934 at a false-positive rate of 0.067, with good transfer across unseen models.
conclusion: Attnlocate effectively localizes behavior-guiding instructions in LLM agents, enabling dynamic adjudication of malicious invocation attempts, and supports authority policy adaptation without retraining.

title: Anatomy Of A Scam Call: What 10,000 Real Scam And Spam Calls Reveal About How Phone Scammers Operate
authors: Ethan Traister, Ankit Raj, Jiaqi Gan, Xingyu Shen, Tyler Wu, Yuchen Zhou, Tommy Duong, Kidus Zewde, Siying Chen, Simiao Ren
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Telephone fraud is pervasive and costly, but its inner workings are rarely observed at scale. We analyze a complete corpus of 10,211 inbound scam and spam calls -- 913 hours of audio and 330,956 transcribed turns from 5,780 distinct numbers -- collected over 54 days by an AI voice-agent honeypot that answered callers and kept them talking, and introduced in a companion data descriptor. We separate outright scams, which solicit sensitive information, from the larger stream of predatory but legal lead generation ("spam") that feeds them. Scam operations keep office hours (6.6x more calls per weekday than weekend day); thousands of disposable numbers run a small catalog of recycled scripts (thirty opening clusters, half the traffic in the top five); and callers solicit identity anchors -- a home address and a date of birth -- far more often than payment credentials, pressing through persistence and manufactured authority rather than overt threats. Our central experiment asks: does it matter who picks up? Every seeded lead carried one of ten fictitious identities drawn uniformly at random, so the identity a fraud operation reaches is fixed before the caller exists. Across 1,823 randomized calls, scammers spent about 15% more conversational turns per decade of the target's apparent age (rate ratio 1.15, 95% CI 1.08-1.23; randomization p = 0.005) -- yet what they asked for did not change (26.3% of calls reached a request for sensitive information; odds ratio 0.99 per decade, 95% CI 0.90-1.08). A second experiment casts early detection as a benchmark: from a scammer's opening lines alone, on a caller-disjoint split, escalation is predictable at 0.72 ROC-AUC from the first line and 0.87 by the eighth, and a plain bag-of-words classifier matches a fine-tuned on-device language model. Telephone fraud emerges as a templated industry that varies how hard it works a target, but not what it wants.
tldr: This paper analyzes a large corpus of real scam and spam calls to understand how phone scammers operate, revealing patterns in their behavior and target selection.
motivation: Telephone fraud is pervasive and costly, but its inner workings are rarely observed at scale, so the authors aim to analyze a large dataset of calls to uncover operational tactics.
method: They used an AI voice-agent honeypot to collect 10,211 inbound scam and spam calls over 54 days, including 913 hours of audio and 330,956 transcribed turns. They conducted randomized experiments with fictitious identities and trained machine learning models to predict escalation from opening lines.
result: Scammers maintain office hours, use recycled scripts, and prioritize identity anchors (address, date of birth) over payment credentials. They spend more effort on older targets but do not change what they ask for. Escalation can be predicted with 0.72 ROC-AUC from the first line and 0.87 by the eighth.
conclusion: Telephone fraud is a templated industry that varies how hard it works a target, but not what it wants, and early detection is feasible with simple classifiers.

title: A Non-CDCL Sat Solver With Early Conflict Detection: The Watched-Literal-Based Csfloc Solver
authors: G\'abor Kusper
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: CSFLOC is a non-CDCL SAT decision procedure based on counting subsumed full-length ordered clauses. The classical CSFLOC loop traverses the ordered space of full-length clauses by a monotone counter: if the current full-length clause is not subsumed by the input formula, its negation is a satisfying assignment; otherwise, a subsuming clause determines a counter jump. The main bottleneck is the repeated search for such a subsuming clause. This paper presents CSFLOC-WL, and its current implementation CSFLOC-WL3, in which this search is replaced by watched-literal prefix propagation over the negation of the current full-length clause represented by the counter. The central mechanism is early conflict detection: if propagation under a common prefix derives opposite unit consequences for the same variable, then the two reason clauses are resolved immediately and the resolvent is used as a new counter-jump cause. The resulting solver is not a CDCL solver: it has no CDCL decision tree, no restart policy, and no first-UIP backjumping loop. It remains a counter-guided full-length-clause-counting solver, but it imports the watched-literal data structure and reason clauses as engineering tools for discovering jumps. Experiments on selected UNSAT SATLIB instances compare CSFLOC-WL3 with CSFLOC21TU and CaDiCaL 3.0.0. The results are mixed: CSFLOC-WL3 is strong on several random 3-SAT instances near the random-3-SAT satisfiability threshold, whereas CSFLOC21TU remains faster on several structured cases, apparently because it contains a more mature cache mechanism that is not yet present in CSFLOC-WL3.
tldr: This paper introduces a SAT solver, CSFLOC-WL3, that uses watched-literal propagation and early conflict detection to improve a non-CDCL counting-based decision procedure, showing mixed performance against existing solvers.
motivation: The classical CSFLOC solver is bottlenecked by repeated searches for subsuming clauses; the authors aim to accelerate this search using watched literals and resolution-based jump causes.
method: The solver replaces subsumption search with watched-literal prefix propagation over the negation of the current full-length clause, and uses early conflict detection to resolve reason clauses and derive new counter-jump causes.
result: Experiments on UNSAT SATLIB instances show mixed results: CSFLOC-WL3 performs well on random 3-SAT near the satisfiability threshold but is slower on structured cases, likely due to a missing cache mechanism present in CSFLOC21TU.
conclusion: The new approach demonstrates potential but requires further optimization, particularly in caching, to compete with mature solvers like CaDiCaL.

title: Do System Prompts Leave Behavioral Fingerprints? A Large-Scale Empirical Study Of Clone Detection Via Output Similarity
authors: Linghan Chen, Yudong Gao, Jiyao Wang, Kaiyan Ji, Honglong Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: System prompts can be extracted from commercial LLMs with over 80\% success and redeployed at zero cost, yet a prompt owner has no way to verify whether a suspected deployment is a clone. We propose Black-Box Behavioral Fingerprinting (BBF): the prompt owner registers a behavioral signature from model outputs and later tests whether a suspect deployment matches that signature more closely than an unrelated baseline. BBF requires only black-box API access. Through a large-scale study (4 model families, 8 benchmarks, 288{,}000 responses), we find that prompt choice explains 24.4\% of output variance and same-model detection reaches AUC 0.876. Cross-model performance is bounded by detector identity, with off-diagonal AUC ranging from 0.845 (Claude as detector) down to 0.665 (Qwen) and overall mean 0.725. BBF resists non-adaptive prompt paraphrasing (AUC [MATH]) and is robust to imperfect extraction, but a single-sentence formal-tone prefix can collapse detection on short structured outputs (MNLI 0.978 [MATH] 0.547), isolating style-invariant detection as the key open problem. Diagnostic Query Optimization, a zero-cost query selection rule, adds [MATH] to cross-model AUC.
tldr: Proposes Black-Box Behavioral Fingerprinting (BBF) to detect cloned LLM deployments by comparing output similarity based on system prompt behavioral signatures.
motivation: System prompts can be extracted and redeployed, but owners lack a way to verify suspected clones.
method: Introduces BBF, which registers a behavioral signature from model outputs and tests suspect deployments against it using black-box API access, validated via a large-scale study across multiple model families.
result: Prompt choice explains significant output variance, and BBF achieves high AUC for same-model detection, with cross-model performance varying by detector identity.
conclusion: BBF is effective but vulnerable to style changes; style-invariant detection remains an open problem.

title: Comparison Invariants For Verifying Control Invariance
authors: Andr\'e Platzer Promit Panja
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Control invariance validates that dynamical systems have a control input that preserves a given property at all times. This paper introduces a set of sound axioms and proof rules in differential dynamic logic (dL) that enable verification of control invariance. First, the scalar and vector comparison principles, relating a system of differential equations to a comparison system such that invariance properties can be established more easily, are axiomatized in dL. This axiomatization primarily utilizes differential ghosts, which are proof-theoretic generalizations of comparison systems. Next, with the comparison principles serving as the basis, comparison invariants are introduced, and sound axioms and proof rules are derived. Comparison invariants reduce the question of control invariance to a functional inequality on its Lie derivative for a suitable class of functions, moreover, the right choice of function can result in decidable arithmetic. Furthermore, the perennially popular control barrier functions (CBFs) used in safety-critical control are shown to be a special instance of comparison invariants. This yields an axiomatization of CBFs that leads to a dedicated set of proof rules. The rules allow for the verification of CBFs, which are traditionally used for synthesizing safe controllers without verification. Lastly, comparison invariants are shown to unify several other safety verification techniques, including Darboux invariants and differential invariants, further cementing their versatility.
tldr: This paper introduces comparison invariants and axiomatizes them in differential dynamic logic, unifying control barrier functions and other safety verification techniques for dynamical systems.
motivation: To provide sound and complete proof rules for verifying control invariance in safety-critical systems, which is traditionally done without verification.
method: Utilizes differential ghosts to axiomatize comparison principles, then derives comparison invariants and proof rules, showing control barrier functions as a special case.
result: Presents sound axioms and proof rules that reduce control invariance to functional inequalities on Lie derivatives, and demonstrates unification with Darboux and differential invariants.
conclusion: Comparison invariants offer a versatile and decidable method for verifying safety properties in control systems.

title: Fair Allocation With Optional Selling
authors: Yotam Gafni Uriel Feige
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider fair allocation of indivisible goods in a setting in which agents have subjective valuation functions over the set of goods, and in addition, goods may be sold at given market prices. In this setting, a fair allocation involves {deciding which goods to sell, how to allocate the unsold goods, and how to divide the money received from the sold goods.} We adapt to this setting the definitions of share-based fairness notions, such as the maximin share (MMS) and the truncated proportional share (TPS), and comparison-based fairness notions such as EF1 and EFX (which we adapt to SEF1 and SEFX). We show the following results when the utility of each agent is additive both over goods and over money. With two agents, there are allocations that are simultaneously MMS and SEFX. With three agents, there are instances in which no allocation gives every agent more than [MATH]-MMS. With any number of agents, there are [MATH]-MMS allocations. There also are allocations that are simultaneously SEFX and [MATH]-TPS. This latter ratio is best possible, even without the SEFX requirement.
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes fair allocation of indivisible goods with the option to sell items at market prices, adapting standard fairness notions to this setting.
motivation: To extend fair division concepts to scenarios where goods can be sold, and to study the existence of fair allocations under such conditions.
method: The authors adapt share-based and comparison-based fairness notions (MMS, TPS, EF1, EFX) to the selling setting, and provide existence results via constructive and impossibility arguments.
result: They show that with two agents, MMS and SEFX are compatible; with three agents, no allocation can guarantee more than a fraction of MMS; and for any number of agents, there exist allocations achieving certain fractions of MMS and SEFX simultaneously, with optimal ratios.
conclusion: The results establish fundamental limits and possibilities for fair allocation with selling, providing guidelines for potential allocation mechanisms.

title: Design And Empirical Characterization Of A Hardware-Realized Turing Machine With Automated Card-Based Programming
authors: Agrima Regmi, Jenish Pant, Pratistha Sapkota, Sanskriti Khatiwada, Binod Sapkota
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physical implementations of Turing Machines remain rare, and existing electromechanical demonstrators and mechanical logic games typically require manual operator intervention, either to trigger each computational step or to reconfigure the state table, or both. This restricts prior physical models to short, operator-paced demonstrations and prevents autonomous execution of extended computations. This paper addresses that gap with a hardware Turing Machine that enables autonomous multi-step execution and reprogrammable optical input without manual intervention between programs. The system integrates an Arduino Mega for state-transition logic, dual NEMA 17 stepper motors for bidirectional tape actuation, infrared reflectance sensors for symbol detection, and an ESP32-CAM-based optical punched-card reader for automated state-table loading. Hole detection under non-uniform illumination used a Breadth-First Search flood-fill algorithm with local adaptive thresholding rather than fixed global thresholding, driven by the memory and library constraints of the ESP32-CAM's microcontroller environment; this improved card-decoding accuracy from 75% to 90% (100% with mechanical card flattening) on a 20-card test set. Mechanical evaluation showed fabrication accuracy of +/-0.15 mm, rack-and-pinion positional error below 0.3 mm across 50 trials, and voltage supply stability within +/-0.2 V under full system load. End-to-end computation was validated against a parallel software simulator (tlang), with all hardware outputs matching the simulated reference exactly across multiple test programs. The system advances prior physical Turing Machine demonstrations through autonomous execution, reprogrammable optical input, and quantitative evaluation of its mechanical, optical, and computational performance.
tldr: This paper presents a hardware-realized Turing machine with automated card-based programming, achieving autonomous execution and high decoding accuracy.
motivation: Existing physical Turing machine demonstrations require manual intervention and cannot run extended computations autonomously, so the authors aim to build a self-contained, reprogrammable hardware implementation.
method: The system integrates an Arduino Mega, stepper motors, infrared sensors, and an ESP32-CAM optical card reader, using a BFS flood-fill algorithm with adaptive thresholding for accurate hole detection and state-table loading.
result: The hardware achieved 90% decoding accuracy (100% with flattening), mechanical precision within ±0.15 mm, positional error <0.3 mm, and matched a software simulator's outputs exactly on multiple test programs.
conclusion: The work advances physical Turing machine demonstrations by enabling autonomous, multi-step execution with reprogrammable optical input and provides quantitative performance evaluations.

title: Reliability Limits And Decoding For Partial Nanopore Protein Rereads With Persistent State
authors: Hongbin Ni, Haofan Dong, Ozgur B. Akan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repeated observations of one physical object need not constitute independent channel uses. We model partial nanopore protein rereads as a finite-alphabet channel with canonical content, persistent readout, and pass-local coverage and synchronization. For exact compound-pass data, matched inference approaches the equivalence-class canonical posterior, and sitewise excess Bayes risk admits an action-aware achievable exponent. In an aligned specialization, observation-local redraw can cause linear-in-[MATH] growth in true-label negative log-likelihood (NLL). We derive order-[MATH] projection-stability bounds and an exact passwise-fusion diagnostic. On a PASTOR-informed semi-synthetic hard-symbol channel, label-blind deterministic-mixture importance sampling (LB-IS) agrees with exact enumeration at [MATH]. At [MATH], LB-IS meets every prespecified aggregate absolute marginal-posterior and score-agreement criterion against a fixed high-allocation reference in three selected conditions. Joint agreement holds for the representative and high-NLL conditions, while the near-zero condition remains inconclusive. Exact [MATH] benchmarks identify order 4 as the smallest tested common cap. At target scale, the reference supports selected unprojected functionals, while neither order 4 nor 5 attains joint agreement, defining a tested finite-memory boundary. Across 16 cells, the order-4 shared branch lowers NLL by 0.033-0.224 nats per residue relative to pass-local.
tldr: This paper models nanopore protein rereads as a finite-alphabet channel with persistent state and analyzes decoding reliability limits.
motivation: To understand and improve decoding for nanopore protein sequencing when repeated reads are not independent due to persistent state effects.
method: The authors model partial nanopore protein rereads as a channel with canonical content, persistent readout, and pass-local coverage/synchronization, then derive bounds, diagnostics, and propose label-blind deterministic-mixture importance sampling (LB-IS) for inference.
result: They find that order-4 shared branch is the smallest tested common cap, reduces NLL, and LB-IS meets agreement criteria in most conditions.
conclusion: The paper provides theoretical and practical insights into decoding for nanopore protein rereads with persistent state, establishing reliability limits and testing boundaries.

title: Next-generation O-ran Edge: Energy-aware Joint Placement And Migration Of Cloud-Native Functions
authors: Nguyen Phuc Tran, Brigitte Jaumard, Oscar Delgado
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The transition toward Open Radio Access Networks (O-RANs) is reshaping how cellular infrastructure is deployed, managed, and optimized. This paper investigates the energy-aware joint placement and migration of cloud-native functions (CNFs) in an O-RAN edge cloud. We consider both a Single-CU-UP association model and a slice-aware Multi-CU-UP relaxation, in which distinct slice-flow groups of the same distributed unit (DU) may be assigned to different Centralized Unit User Plane (CU-UP) processing targets under one Centralized Unit Control Plane (CU-CP). For brevity, these scenarios are referred to as Single-CU and Multi-CU, respectively; Multi-CU never denotes multiple CU-CP associations. We formulate the problem as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) that minimizes server, transmission, wake-up, and migration energy while satisfying server-resource capacities and one-way delay requirements over the F1 user-plane interface (F1-U) between each DU and its selected CU-UP in a fat-tree edge data center. To improve computational scalability, we also develop a deterministic k-means-based heuristic that approximates the MILP decisions without requiring repeated exact optimization. Over the evaluated 24-hour workload, the theoretical Multi-CU relaxation reduces modeled energy consumption by 5.7% relative to the Single-CU baseline. For the Multi-CU case, the proposed heuristic remains within approximately 9.7% of the proposed MILP, demonstrating a favorable trade-off between energy efficiency and computational tractability.
tldr: This paper addresses energy-aware placement and migration of cloud-native functions in O-RAN edge clouds, proposing a MILP and a heuristic to minimize energy consumption.
motivation: The shift to O-RAN introduces flexibility but also energy challenges; optimizing placement and migration of CNFs can reduce energy use while meeting delay and capacity constraints.
method: Formulates the problem as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) for Single-CU and Multi-CU models, and develops a deterministic k-means-based heuristic for scalability.
result: The Multi-CU relaxation reduces modeled energy by 5.7% vs. Single-CU, and the heuristic stays within 9.7% of the MILP for Multi-CU.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a favorable trade-off between energy efficiency and computational tractability for O-RAN edge deployments.

title: On The Dirichlet-to-Neumann Conformal Invariant Of Bounded Planar Domains
authors: Alexey Kokotov, Dmitrii Korikov, Marina Nenasheva
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using an analogue of Mandelstam-Giddings-Wolpert diagrams, we introduce a new canonical representative of the conformal class of a bounded domain of arbitrary connectivity in [MATH] as a flat conical surface with geodesic boundary (a "truncated light-cone diagram", simply LC-diagram in the sequel). The space of these diagrams can be provided with natural coordinates. We derive variational formulas for the determinant of the Dirichlet boundary problem on a LC-diagram with respect to these coordinates. Then passing to the Schottky double of the LC-diagram, making use of the Burghelea-Friedlander-Kappeler formula and the known variational formulas for determinants of Laplacians on the moduli space of holomorphic differentials lead to an explicit computation of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DN) conformal invariant [MATH] (here [MATH] is the DN operator on the boundary, [MATH], of a multi-connected domain and [MATH] is the length of the boundary). The resulting formula (which uses the periods of the Schottky double of the domain only) presents a conspicuously elementary counterpart to the formulas of Guillarmou and Guillop\'e who had expressed the DN invariant through the Ruelle and Selberg zeta-functions. Our formula agrees with the recent result of Wentworth on the asymptotics of the DN invariant as all the boundary components except one shrink, we have used this result to fix the undetermined constant of integration in our formula.
tldr: This paper introduces a new canonical representative for conformal classes of bounded planar domains using truncated light-cone diagrams and derives an explicit formula for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann conformal invariant.
motivation: The authors aim to provide an elementary counterpart to existing formulas for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann conformal invariant, which is important in conformal geometry and spectral theory.
method: They use an analogue of Mandelstam-Giddings-Wolpert diagrams to represent bounded domains as flat conical surfaces with geodesic boundary, then apply the Burghelea-Friedlander-Kappeler formula and variational formulas for determinants on moduli spaces.
result: They obtain an explicit computation of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann conformal invariant in terms of the periods of the Schottky double, agreeing with the asymptotics of Wentworth when all but one boundary components shrink.
conclusion: The work provides a new, more elementary formula for a classical conformal invariant, enhancing the understanding of bounded planar domains from a spectral geometry perspective.

title: Horizon: A Read-Efficient Firmware For Dna Storage With Horizontal Layout
authors: Alex Sensintaffar, Roop Kiran, Yang Chen, Mai Zheng, Bingzhe Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: DNA storage is a promising medium for long-term archiving, but its read performance is limited by coarse-grained random access. Existing random-access DNA storage designs suffer from high read amplification because their sequential layouts co-locate frequently and infrequently accessed data under the same primer pair, where any read must retrieve all associated strands even when only a small fraction is needed. We present HORIZON, a read-efficient allocation policy for DNA block devices that reduces read amplification through activity-aware horizontal placement. HORIZON first introduces a horizontal layout distributing writes round-robin across primer pairs, rather than filling each sequentially. It classifies newly written blocks in the write buffer as active or inactive, tracks recent primer-pair accesses using a sliding-window temperature model, and allocates blocks based on block activity and primer-pair occupancy. Simulations show HORIZON consistently reduces read amplification compared with state-of-the-art schemes across MSR and FIU traces and synthetic filesystem workloads.
tldr: This paper presents HORIZON, a read-efficient allocation policy for DNA storage that reduces read amplification via activity-aware horizontal placement.
motivation: DNA storage offers long-term archiving but suffers from high read amplification due to coarse-grained random access and sequential layouts that co-locate frequently and infrequently accessed data.
method: HORIZON introduces a horizontal layout that distributes writes round-robin across primer pairs, classifies blocks as active/inactive, and uses a sliding-window temperature model to allocate blocks based on activity and occupancy.
result: Simulations show HORIZON consistently reduces read amplification compared to state-of-the-art schemes across MSR, FIU traces, and synthetic filesystem workloads.
conclusion: HORIZON demonstrates a promising approach for improving read efficiency in DNA storage systems, but the work is entirely unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Not All Tokens Are Equal: Region-Aware Consistency Repair Of Backdoors In MLLMs
authors: Jiali Wei, Ming Fan, Mingkun Zhang, Haoyu Wang, Jun Sun, Guoheng Sun, Xiaoning Ren, Haijun Wang, Ting Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: MLLMs are increasingly deployed in user-facing applications, yet they inherit backdoor risks from the pipelines used to construct them: triggers may reside in images, texts, or both. Existing model-level backdoor removal methods, largely designed for conventional classifiers, show limited effectiveness on MLLMs, while MLLM-specific defenses mainly operate at inference time, filtering suspicious inputs without removing the backdoor embedded in the model. To address this gap and eliminate latent backdoors from MLLMs at their source, we present RACER, a model-level repair framework motivated by a key observation: backdoors induce abnormal layer-to-layer evolution in internal representations, which we term the layer-wise inconsistency anomaly. Importantly, this anomaly is modality-dependent, concentrating primarily in the token region encoding the trigger features that the backdoor model actually relies on. RACER therefore decomposes the fused representation into visual and textual token regions, normalizes their layer-wise inconsistency separately, and recomposes them using modality-aware weights over a deep-layer window, yielding a region-aware inconsistency objective that better captures localized backdoor-induced anomalies. Through a min-max optimization, this objective drives worst-case perturbation synthesis and adversarial fine-tuning against the resulting perturbation to repair the model, suppressing the deep representational directional shifts on which backdoor behaviors rely. RACER requires only 100 clean samples and no knowledge of the trigger, attack objective, or even whether the input model contains a backdoor. Evaluations on three open-source MLLMs across 36 backdoor settings spanning image, text, and multimodal triggers show that RACER reduces the average ASR to 1.1%, reaching 0% in 32 settings, while preserving clean-task utility on both backdoor and clean models.
tldr: RACER is a model-level backdoor repair framework for multimodal large language models that leverages region-aware layer-wise inconsistency to detect and mitigate backdoors while preserving utility.
motivation: Backdoors in MLLMs are a growing security threat, and existing removal methods are ineffective or only operate at inference time. The paper aims to eliminate latent backdoors at the source.
method: RACER decomposes fused representations into visual and textual token regions, normalizes layer-wise inconsistency separately, and uses a min-max optimization to synthesize worst-case perturbations and fine-tune the model adversarially.
result: On three open-source MLLMs across 36 backdoor settings, RACER reduces average attack success rate to 1.1% (0% in 32 settings) while preserving clean-task utility.
conclusion: RACER effectively repairs backdoors in MLLMs without knowing trigger details, requiring only 100 clean samples, offering a practical model-level defense.

title: Spatiotemporal Organization In Bike-sharing Systems Using Gravity Model Parameters
authors: Hanbo Zhang, Qi Rao, Bo Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravity models describe bike-sharing origin-destination (OD) flows as increasing with origin and destination activity and decreasing with distance. Yet how these relationships change within a day and across observation areas remains unclear. We examine temporal and spatial variation in origin, destination and distance exponents [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], together with [MATH] and mean absolute error (MAE), across eight bike-sharing systems. Temporal modeling uses sliding windows, while spatial modeling expands a circular area and separates intra-zonal, cross-zonal outflow, cross-zonal inflow and extra-zonal trips. We find recurring patterns across cities: morning and evening peaks differ in origin and destination dependence, while cross-zonal outflow and inflow across the same boundary show opposite changes in their relative origin and destination dependence as radius increases. Model performance and distance dependence also vary with time and radius. A full-day, citywide fit therefore combines time periods and flow types with different gravity relationships.
tldr: This paper analyzes spatiotemporal variation in gravity model parameters for bike-sharing systems, which is unrelated to quantum information or related physics.
motivation: The study aims to understand how origin, destination, and distance dependencies in bike-sharing trip flows change over time and space.
method: The authors apply gravity models to eight bike-sharing systems, using sliding windows for temporal variation and expanding circular areas with trip-type segmentation for spatial variation.
result: They find recurring patterns across cities, such as differing morning/evening peaks and opposite changes in cross-zonal outflow versus inflow dependence as radius increases.
conclusion: The findings imply that a full-day, citywide fit combines time periods and flow types with different gravity relationships, highlighting the need for context-specific modeling.

title: Design And Numerical Performance Analysis Of Efficient Ag3TaX4 (x = S, Se, Te) Thin Film Solar Cells
authors: Md. Nahid Hasan, Tanvir Ahmed, Md. Abdur Rashid, Tanzina Rahman, Dinesh Pathak, Jaker Hossain
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silver-based ternary chalcogenides have recently emerged as promising absorber materials for thin film photovoltaics. Nevertheless, their photovoltaic performance in complete device architectures has not yet been systematically explored. In this work, three-dimensional (3D) n-CdS/p-Ag3TaX4 (X = S, Se, Te)/p+-GeS thin-film solar cells have been designed and numerically investigated using the Semiconductor Module of COMSOL Multiphysics. Herein, the various performance matrices of the proposed devices have been analysed in accordance with the changing of depth, carrier, and defect concentration in each layer of the structures. The optimized Ag3TaS4-based device delivers a power conversion efficiency, PCE of 24.66%, open circuit voltage, VOC of 1.4V, short circuit current density, JSC of 20.68 mA/cm2, and fill factor, FF of 85.16%. The Ag3TaSe4-based solar cell exhibits the PCE of 28.1% with VOC = 1.19V, JSC = 27.0 mA/cm2, and FF = 87.44%. The Ag3TaTe4 solar device shows a PCE of 27.56% with a VOC of 0.88 V, JSC of 36.14 mA/cm2, fill factor of 86.65%. These results provide a deeper insight into device operation and offer practical design guidelines for fabricating efficient Ag3TaX4 (X = S, Se, T e)-based novel next-generation solar cells.
tldr: This paper numerically simulates Ag3TaX4 (X=S, Se, Te) thin-film solar cells using COMSOL Multiphysics, reporting high power conversion efficiencies.
motivation: To explore silver-based ternary chalcogenides as promising absorber materials for next-generation thin-film photovoltaics and provide design guidelines.
method: Three-dimensional numerical simulations were performed using the Semiconductor Module of COMSOL Multiphysics, varying depth, carrier, and defect concentrations in each layer.
result: Optimized devices yield PCEs of 24.66% (Ag3TaS4), 28.1% (Ag3TaSe4), and 27.56% (Ag3TaTe4) with associated open-circuit voltages, short-circuit currents, and fill factors.
conclusion: The results offer practical design insights for fabricating efficient Ag3TaX4-based solar cells, but the work is unrelated to the user's research directions.

title: Emergence Of Stigmergic Transport In Granular Environments
authors: F. W\'ery, F. N. Pinan Basualdo, B. Gorissen, N. Vandewalle
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that stigmergic path formation emerges in a deformable environment through the interplay between environmental memory and geometrical crowding. Using experiments with robotic random walkers together with a minimal stochastic model, we demonstrate the onset of persistent self-reinforced transport pathways above a critical packing fraction [MATH], where environmental memory enhances walker mobility. As the jamming transition [MATH] is approached, increasing crowding progressively suppresses this transport enhancement despite the persistence of environmental memory. The resulting non-monotonic behavior reveals an optimal transport regime well below jamming. More generally, our work establishes how active agents can collectively build transport networks through purely mechanical interactions with a deformable substrate.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the emergence of stigmergic transport pathways in granular environments via robotic walkers and a stochastic model, revealing an optimal transport regime below jamming.
motivation: To understand how active agents can collectively build transport networks through purely mechanical interactions with a deformable substrate, without central control.
method: Experiments with robotic random walkers on a deformable granular medium, combined with a minimal stochastic model to analyze the onset and persistence of self-reinforced paths as a function of packing fraction.
result: Persistent transport pathways emerge above a critical packing fraction, but approach the jamming transition, crowding suppresses transport enhancement, yielding non-monotonic behavior with an optimal regime.
conclusion: Active agents can autonomously create transport networks through mechanical interactions, with environmental memory and crowding interplay determining efficiency.

title: On The Convergence Rate Of The Duality Gap In The Generalized Frank-Wolfe Method Under The Weak Growth Condition
authors: Renbo Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the convergence rate of certain sequence of the duality gaps in the generalized Frank-Wolfe method, under certain regime of the weak growth condition proposed in Pe\~na (2023). Our analysis leverages a recursion lemma that may be of independent interest.
tldr: This paper analyzes the convergence rate of the duality gap in the generalized Frank-Wolfe method under a weak growth condition.
motivation: To understand the convergence behavior of duality gaps in the generalized Frank-Wolfe method, which is important for algorithm performance analysis.
method: The analysis uses a recursion lemma to study the sequence of duality gaps, leveraging the weak growth condition proposed by Peña (2023).
result: Provides convergence rate guarantees for the duality gap sequence under the assumed regime of the weak growth condition.
conclusion: The paper contributes to the theoretical understanding of the generalized Frank-Wolfe method, though it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Weak-type Characterizations Of Sobolev And Bounded Variation Spaces On Metric Measure Spaces
authors: Tuomas P. Hyt\"onen, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan, Yirui Zhao

method: Introduces a localized Bourgain-Brezis-Mironescu type characterization, using weak-type norms based on differences or mean oscillations to characterize Sobolev and BV spaces.

title: Cycle Time Minimization For The Simple Assembly Line Balancing Problem Under Peak Power Constraints
authors: Bao Gia Hoang, Tuyen van Kieu, Khanh van To
abstract: ArXiv:2608.24779v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Peak power limits restrict concurrent tasks and may increase assembly-line cycle time. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to minimize cycle time for the simple assembly line balancing problem type 2 (SALBP-2) with a fixed number of workstations and a fixed limit on total instantaneous power. An exact satisfiability (SAT) method finds feasible schedules, searches systematically for shorter cycles, and proves optimality when possible. Two reproducible formulas define looser and tighter power limits for 72 cases based on the standard SALBP library, with Gurobi and CPLEX providing commercial MIP and CP comparisons. Relative to standard SALBP-2 optima, the two limits increase the best-known cycle time by 16.49% and 61.02% on average. The best-performing SAT configurations find a feasible solution for every case, solve more cases to optimality than each commercial solver, and when both prove optimality, are almost always faster under the reported settings.
tldr: This paper proposes a SAT-based exact method to minimize cycle time for the simple assembly line balancing problem type 2 under peak power constraints, demonstrating effectiveness against commercial solvers.
motivation: Peak power limits restrict concurrent tasks and can increase assembly-line cycle time, but this specific optimization problem (SALBP-2 with power limits) has not been previously studied.
method: The authors develop an exact satisfiability (SAT) approach that finds feasible schedules, systematically searches for shorter cycles, and proves optimality when possible. They define two power limit formulas and compare against Gurobi and CPLEX (MIP and CP).
result: The SAT configurations find feasible solutions for all cases, solve more cases to optimality than each commercial solver, and are often faster when both prove optimality.
conclusion: The SAT-based method is effective for cycle time minimization under peak power constraints, offering improvements over commercial solvers in this problem domain.

title: Compositionality In Quantum Reference Frame Perspectives
authors: Esteban Castro-Ruiz Bruna Sahdo
abstract: ArXiv:2608.23698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding a composite system through its constituents is a fundamental practice in physics. In the context of quantum reference frames (QRFs), however, combining the usual quantum-theoretic notion of composition with QRF perspectives gives rise to subtle issues, such as the 'paradox of the third particle'. Here we study in depth how to compose subsystems in QRF perspectives, building on a recent formalism for QRFs [E.Castro-Ruiz and O.Oreshkov, 2025]. We first show how the frames of external observers can be internalised and treated within the framework. This establishes a consistent hierarchy of QRF perspectives, which we use to define the adding and removing of subsystems. We then explain how, owing to the so-called 'extra-particle' degrees of freedom, the formalism gives a consistent treatment of subsystems, avoiding any paradoxes by construction. Consistency then implies that composing subsystems in a QRF perspective differs from, and generalises, the standard quantum-theoretic case. In particular, not every state can be appended in tensor-product form relative to a QRF, and we characterise the set of compatible states. Finally, we introduce 'classicalisation', a procedure that recovers a classical-like perspective from a general QRF. This procedure circumvents the aforementioned state restrictions but carries a different operational meaning, which we study through a concrete example.

authors: Fahad Puthalath, Dipanjan Mandal, Sumanta Kundu

We study the role of cluster shape diversity on jamming properties of the system by systematically controlling the number of distinct shapes used across and within realizations, encompassing both monodisperse and polydisperse model variants. Our large-scale simulations over a broad range of cluster sizes [MATH] show that the jamming density decreases with cluster size as a power-law [MATH]. Both [MATH] and [MATH] are found to depend on the degree of shape diversity, with [MATH] ranging from [MATH] to [MATH]. It is observed that increasing shape polydispersity promotes denser packing. Importantly, the fluctuations of the jamming density exhibit distinct scaling behavior: [MATH] for a fixed pool of cluster shape(s), but remain [MATH]-independent when the pool of shape(s) is refreshed across different realizations. method: Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations of random sequential adsorption of DLA clusters with controlled shape diversity, including monodisperse and polydisperse variants.
